body: “Erect committee to develop funding of General Assembly” Whereas, the General Assembly consists of all teaching elders (TE) who are in good standing in their Presbyteries and Ruling Elders (RE) elected by their Sessions (BCO 14-2), and Whereas, congregations are entitled to two RE representatives for the first 350 communing members or fraction thereof, and one additional RE for each additional 500 communing members or fraction thereof, (BCO 14-2), and Whereas, at the 27th General Assembly the ratio of TE stores was over 2 to 1 (854 to 374), and it has long been the concern of the PCA that there be more RE representation from the congregations, and Whereas, small congregations often lack the financial ability to send one representative let alone two or three, and Whereas, representatives of small congregations often use creative ways to save money and still get to General Assembly meeting, (i.e. sharing rides, using buddy fares on planes, sharing rooms with representatives from other congregations, staying in inexpensive second-class motels, etc.), and Whereas, small congregations may be able to find creative ways to send more than one representative to General Assembly without large increases in travel and lodging costs, (i.e. sharing rides, using buddy fares on planes, sharing rooms, having representatives pay their own travel and meal costs, etc.), and Whereas, the increases in the registration fee for attending the General Assembly is making it more and more difficult for small congregations to send representatives, while large congregations are less impacted by the increases on a per capita basis, and Whereas, this dynamic may lead to an imbalance in representation at the General Assembly, not only between TEs and REs (as already seen), but between large and small congregations, and Whereas, the expenses of representatives to the General Assembly is to be defrayed by the bodies which they represent, (BCO 10-6), and Whereas, the Administrative Committee does incur significant expense in arranging and facilitating the meeting of the General Assembly, and Whereas, the Administrative Committee is to set a registration fee, subject to the approval of the General Assembly, (RAO 9-4), and Whereas, ape rca pita division of the cost is more equitable and in the spirit of Christian love, than a flat rate which does not take into consideration the increased financial liability this causes per capita for small congregations when the flat rate is increased, (i.e. the ratio of increase per ca pita is much greater on small congregations than on large congregations), and Whereas, the bible teaches us to take into consideration the needs of our brethren (cf. Acts 11:29). Therefore Be it Resolved that the 28th General Assembly of the PCA be asked to erect a committee to develop a more equitable method of funding the cost of the Assembly. adopted by the presbytery of new jersey on february 19, 2000. Attested by: /s/ James A. Smith, Stated Clerk

“Condemn the SJC Decision in the John Wood Case” Whereas, Presbyterianism historically has allowed for one General Assembly to condemn the opinion of another General Assembly (M 12GA, p. 140: "A subsequent General Assembly may take a contrary position and condemn the action of a previous Assembly."); and Whereas, the decisions of the Standing Judicial Commission (SJC) are those of the previous General Assembly (BCO 15-4: "and each subsequent Assembly should declare the Standing Judicial Commission as a whole to be is commission”), and Whereas, the General Assembly is bound "to bear testimony against error in doctrine ., injuriously affecting the Church.” (BCO 14-6.a ); and Whereas, the decision oft hes jc in RE Presbyterian Church in America vs. John Wood is evidently flawed, and Whereas, because of the peculiar nature of current PCA judicial process, the General Assembly as such never was able directly to review this decision of the SJC; and Whereas, the decision is flawed in numerous ways, especially in its interpretation of the Constitution; and Whereas, among the errors in Constitutional interpretation are the following: (1) the SJC assumes that a corporate responsibility by a session means that individual members cannot also be held responsible for the action of the session; (2) the SJC assumes that there were no doctrinal issues involved, but merely the action of inviting a woman to fill the pulpit, when there is evidence that Mr. Wood advocates female preaching; (3) the SJC assumes that action by Tennessee Valley Presbytery to vindicate the session of cedar springs presbyterian Church, Knoxville, Tennessee, automatically clears Mr. Wood, (4) the SJC forcibly recused members oft hes jc from Ascension, Calvary, and Western Carolina Presbyteries, based on the allegation that these Presbyteries were parties to the case, whereas in point of fact, ina case of original jurisdiction, the "original and only parties ina case of process are the accuser and the accused. The accuser is always the Presbyterian Church in America" (BCO 31-3), and Whereas, this situation of having a seriously-flawed decision in this judicial case is troubling to the church and is potentially divisive, and Whereas, the god who has called us to peace is not the author of confusion, and Whereas, the Ninth Commandment requires "from the heart, sincerely, freely, clearly, and fully, speaking the truth, and only the truth, in matters of judgment and justice" (WLC, Q/A 144), and Now Therefore, Be it Resolve, that Louisiana Presbytery hereby overtures the 28th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to condemn and to bear testimony against the judgment of the 27th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America regarding the judicial case with respect to the Rev. Mr. John Wood Adopted by Louisiana Presbytery at the 63rd Stated Meeting, Opelousas, Louisiana, on April 15, 2000. Attested by: /s/ James A Jones, jr , Stated Clerk MINORITY REPORT ON RECOMMENDATION 1 OF THE COMMITTEE OF COMMISSIONERS ON BILLS AND OVERTURES That OVERTURE 22 from Louisiana Presbytery be answered in the negative. Grounds: 1. we are in agreement with the advice of the CCB in its response to: Reference 1 from the presbytery of western carolina (pp. 68-70); Reference 2 from the presbytery of the ascension (p. 70), Constitutional Inquiry 1 from the presbytery of the ascension (p. 73),

2. BCO 34-1 has two prerequisites which must be met before the matter of TE john Woods/Cedar Springs PCA can properly be before the GA. The SJC has determined that Tennessee Valley Presbytery has indeed acted. Therefore, since the first prerequisite has not been met, the GA has no jurisdiction in this matter. 3. The Resolutions from the three Presbyteries were directed by the Presbyteries to the GA and were considered by the GA via the SJC. 4. The GA has established the SJC as the Assembly’s normal process for handling cases of this kind (BCO 15-4, “The General Assembly shall erect a Standing Judicial Commission to which it shall commit all judicial cases within its jurisdiction"). 5. The GA via the SJC found these resolutions to be out of order because the grounds upon which they sought the GA to act via the SJC were wrong, namely the Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the matter of TE John Wood and his Session. 6. The SJC also noted that while some members of the Tennessee Valley Presbytery protested the Presbytery’s investigation, no members of the Presbytery sought to bring that protest to the SJC via a complaint. 7. As the SJC has acted on behalf of the GA it would be quite inappropriate for the GA and the SJC to take this case up a second time. Further, it would be quite inappropriate for the GA, in effect, to investigate a TE a second time when he has been cleared of wrong doing by his Presbytery. Such a second investigation would amount to an act of double jeopardy. 8. In addition, the BCO and the SJC Manual provide for only the most limited circumstances for a case that has been considered by the SJC to then be considered by the GA. That process requires that one-third of the SJC members prepare a minority report (BCO 15-5-c). It is clearly the intention of the BCO that a case once considered by the SJC cannot be again considered by the GA. 9. Further, it would appear that for this overture or for the Bills and Overtures Committee recommendation to be adopted that it would require an amendment to the BCO to set aside BCO 15 and a motion made to suspend the RAO (Article 15 and the SJC Manual). Committee Members Joining in this Minority Report: TE Craig Childs, Evangel TE Fredric Mau, Palmetto TE Stephen Estock, Southeast Alabama TE Charles McGowan, Nashville TE Bill Lamkin, North Florida RE Claude Roberts, South Texas 2. That OVERTURE 9 from the Presbytery of the Ascension (“Amend BCO 24-1”) be answered by referring the overture back to the Presbytery. Adopted Grounds: The pending amendment to BCO 24-1 has now received the approval of a sufficient number of Presbyteries. A change adopted so recently by the Assembly ought not to be reviewed again until the Church has had time to practically assess its effect. There is a presumptive virtue in settled law.

source: OVERTURE 9 From the Presbytery of the Ascension
body: “Amend BCO 24-1” Whereas, the 26th GA adopted a proposed amendment to BCO 24-1 (printed below); and Whereas, the grounds cited by Central Carolina Presbytery (which brought the original overture) and by the Bills & Overtures Committee were that the requirements of BCO 24-1 requiring (1) that there be at least one month’s prior notice of a meeting for electing officers and (2) that Session inform the congregation before election day of those eligible for election “can place undue time constraints on the Session.” (M26GA, pp. 208-209); and Whereas, that amendment is still pending because there were not sufficient presbyteries voting in favor of it (M27GA, pp. 58-60); and Whereas, at least 13 presbyteries have voted against this proposed amendment (M27GA, pp. 58-60); and Whereas, the reasons for the negative votes seem to be tied to (1) the absence in the new language of a clear statement that it is the Session which must examine the candidates and (2) confusion regarding the meaning of the second paragraph of the amendment [i.e., does the “30 days” requirement mean that the names of eligible nominees must be reported to the congregation at the time of the call for the meeting (which the order of the events in 24-1 seems to imply) or does it simply speak to the required notice for the meeting while leaving the Session the discretion as to when to report the names of eligible nominees (and thus allowing the Session to not report those names prior to the meeting if it so desires)?]; and Whereas, it seems to us that it is reasonable to require 30 days notice of a meeting for an election, but not necessarily 30 days notice of who are eligible nominees; and Whereas, it seems reasonable to us to require that the names of eligible nominees be given to the congregation before the day of election; and Whereas, it would seem to be good stewardship to seek to address those concerns before the proposed amendment is finally adopted, thus avoiding the need for future amendments; Therefore Be it Resolved, that the Presbytery of the Ascension overture the 28th General Assembly to adopt the following language in lieu of the pending amendment to BCO 24-1: [Additions to the pending proposal are underlined, while deletions are struck through.] A. Substitute the following for the first paragraph: 24-1. Every church shall elect persons to the office of ruling elder and deacon in the following manner: At such times as determined by the Session, communicant members of the congregation may submit names to the Session, keeping in mind that each prospective officer shall be an active male member who meets the qualifications set forth in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1. After the close of the nomination period nominees for the office of ruling elder and/or deacon shall receive instruction in the qualifications and work of the office. Each nominee shall then be examined by the Session in: [NOTE: continue with the areas of examination.] B. Substitute for the second paragraph (i.e., “The Session shall examine...”) the following: If there are candidates eligible for election, the Session shall report to the congregation those eligible, giving at least 30 days prior notice of the time and place of a congregational meeting for election. The Session shall give at least 30 days prior notice of the time and place of the congregational meeting for elections. It shall also report to the congregation before election day those eligible for election. And be it Further Resolved that, if the Committee on Constitutional Business and the Bills & Overtures Committee agree that the revised language has merit, that the latter be permitted to offer a partial report at the time of voting on the adoption of the pending amendment so that commissioners may have the opportunity to adopt this revised language as a proposed amendment before voting on whether or not to finally adopt the amendment which is currently before the presbyteries. Adopted at the January Stated Meeting of the Presbytery of the Ascension on January 29, 2000. Attested by: /s/ Frederick R. Neikirk, Stated Clerk 3. That OVERTURE 2 from Grace Presbytery (“Grant Full Constitutional Status to the Entire Directory of Worship”) be answered in the negative. Adopted Grounds: The procedure suggested by Overture 2 seems to indicate that the Directory for Worship can be given full constitutional status by a mere vote of the General Assembly. However, establishing “full constitutional status and weight” would have to be accomplished according to the proper precedent-setting procedure employed with respect to Chapters 56-58 (cf. M8GA (1980), p. 118; M9GA (1981), pp. 137-142).

“Grant Full Constitutional Status to the Entire Directory of Worship” Whereas, it has always been the practice of Presbyterian denominations around the world to include some form of a directory for the public worship of God within their constitutional standards; and Whereas, the public worship of God is a principal, and the most visible, act performed by the Church of the Lord Jesus Christ; and Whereas, the Bible enjoins all Christians to worship in a fitting and orderly way (1 Corinthians 14:40); and Whereas, the matter of public worship is one of considerable debate and increasing tension within the Presbyterian Church in America; and Whereas, the current Directory for Worship of the Presbyterian Church in America is only “an approved guide” and “does not have the force of law and is not to be considered obligatory” in most of its parts; Therefore, be it resolved that Grace Presbytery overture the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to rescind the current prefatory statement to the Directory For Worship, and in so doing grant the Directory for Worship full constitutional status and weight. Adopted this 11th day of May, in the year of our Lord, nineteen hundred, ninety- nine, by the presbytery of grace in its ninety-fourth stated meeting, at Hazlehurst, Mississippi. Attested by: /s/ E. C. Case, Stated Clerk 5. That OVERTURE 12 from Potomac Presbytery (“Prohibit Women from Preaching in Public Worship”) be answered in the affirmative as amended Add a new clause at BCO 12.5d., after the words “Bible study groups;”, as follows: to encourage the women in the church to hold meetings and give instruction appropriate to their calling (e.g. Titus 2:3-5), while prohibiting women from expounding ©f and preaching the word of god a san ordinance of public worship (cf. BCO 4-4; 53-2), as this is clearly forbidden in Scripture (1 Tim. 2:11-12). Adopted as amended Grounds: The overture is very narrowly drafted, applicable by virtue of the parenthetical only to the expounding and preaching of the word of god a san ordinance of public worship (i.e., the sermon) in the local church. Making this restriction explicit will protect and proclaim the well-grounded biblical consensus that exists in the PCA on this matter.

“Prohibit Women from Preaching in Public Worship” Whereas, questions have been raised across the church concerning the legitimate role of women in the PCA, and whether the constitution of the PCA is sufficiently explicit to guard against unbiblical practices with respect to the ministry of women in our churches; Therefore, Potomac Presbytery respectfully overtures the 28th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to proceed to the amendment of Book of Church Order to the following effect: add a new clause at BCO 12.5d., after the words “Bible study groups;”, as follows: to encourage the women in the church to hold meetings and give instruction appropriate to their calling (e.g. Titus 2:3-5), while prohibiting women from expounding or preaching the word of god a san ordinance of public worship (cf. BCO 4-4; 53-2), as this is clearly forbidden in Scripture (1 Tim. 2:11-12); Adopted by Potomac Presbytery at the 41st Stated Meeting, February 12, 2000. Attested by: /s/ Richard R. Larson, Stated Clerk S. That OVERTURE 10 from the presbytery of mississippi valley (“Restrict Preaching or Exhorting to Qualified Men Only”) be answered in the negative (See also Majority Rationale, p. 80 and Minority Reports, p 87, 89) Adopted Grounds: The overture asks the Assembly to replace the language in question If the request is taken literally, it can only be acceded to if the views argued in the minority report of the CCB are correct, and the DFW in this section is not a part of the Constitution. But in that case, there is little point in the adjustment, since the affected document is counted as what amounts to an in thesi statement of a previous Assembly. If the request is taken loosely, as a request for the Assembly to initiate the Constitutional process for amending the BCO, it can only be acceded to if the views argued by the majority of the CCB are correct, and the section is part of the Constitution. But in that case, the matter is better addressed by Overture 12.

source: OVERTURE 10 from the presbytery of mississippi valley
body: “Restrict Preaching or Exhorting to Qualified Men Only” Whereas, the Westminster Confession of Faith, Chapter XXI, paragraph 5 discusses the elements of corporate worship, and “sound preaching. . .” is an element of corporate worship, and Whereas, god ordained men to bethe spiritual leaders of israel (Ex. 18: 17-26), and Whereas, the priesthood of israel was composed only of the sons of aaron (Ex. 28: 1-4), and Whereas, the apostles of Jesus, used of god to establish the new covenant Church for our Lord, were all men (Mt. 10: 1-4), and Whereas, the Bible forbids women to teach or exercise authority over men (I Tim. 2: 11-15), and Whereas, Larger Catechism, question 158 states: “.. .the word of god is to be preached only by such as are sufficiently gifted and also duly approved and called to that office,” and Whereas, God forbids ordained office to women (I Tim. 3: 2,12, Titus 1: 6), and Whereas, the entire bible teaches the principle of covenant heads hip of men over women (I Cor. 11: 3), a principle which is usurped when women exhort or instruct men in the church, Let it Therefore Be Resolved that Mississippi Valley Presbytery overture the 28th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to replace Book of Church Order paragraph 53-6, which currently reads: “No persons hall be invited to preach in any of the churches under our care without the consent of the Session, ” with the following: “Only qualified men with the consent of the sessions hall be invited to preach/exhort in any of the churches under our care. ” adopted at the winter stated meeting of the presbytery of mississippi valley on February 15, 2000. Attested by: /s/R oger G. Collins, Stated Clerk 6. That OVERTURE 15 from New Jersey Presbytery (“Revise BCO 56-5 Regarding ‘Our Holy Religion’”) be answered by referring the matter back to New Jersey Presbytery to perfect the form (e.g., RAO 10-11) and resubmit if they so desire. Adopted

“Revise BCO 56-5 Regarding ‘Our Holy Religion.’” Whereas, the first paragraph of *The Directory for the Worship of God*, states that “BCO 56, 57 and 58 have been given full constitutional authority by the Eleventh General Assembly after being submitted to the Presbyteries and receiving the necessary two-thirds (2/3) approval of the Presbyteries,” and Whereas, BCO 56-5 states, regarding the questions a minister is to ask when doing an infant baptism, “The minister shall then propose the following questions…”, and Whereas, the word “shall” requires the minister to use the specific wording of the questions as recorded in BCO 56-5, and Whereas, in question three the term “our holy religion” is used, and Whereas, in modern English the term “religion” carries with it the idea of a man-made belief system in that there are numerous world religions, and Whereas, Colossians 3:23 specifically uses the term “religion” in a negative sense referring to man-made religion, and Whereas, the BCO 56-5 use of the term “our” also adds to the connection to Colossians 3:23 about religions as being of human origin, and Whereas, the intent of BCO 56-5 is that of encouraging the teaching of the true doctrines given to the Church by the Lord Jesus as revealed in the Bible, Therefore, be it so ordered that the BCO be revised by the following action: Delete the phrase “our holy religion” and add the phrase “the holy Bible”, in BCO 56-5, so that question three will read, in part, “…that you will teach (him) the doctrines of the holy Bible, and…” Not adopted by the Presbytery of New Jersey. [RAO 10-10] Attested by: /s/ James A. Smith, Stated Clerk NOTE: Presbytery did, however, vote to suggest to the Assembly regarding OVERTURE 15 and 16 that the Assembly erect a committee to deal with language and style in the BCO. 7. That OVERTURE 16 from New Jersey Presbytery (“Revise BCO 56-5 Regarding ‘Means of God’s Appointment’”) be answered by referring the matter back to New Jersey Presbytery to perfect the form (e.g., RAO 10-11) and resubmit if they so desire. Adopted

“Revise BCO 56-5 Regarding “Means of God’s Appointment” Whereas, the first paragraph of the directory for the worship of God, states that “BCO 56, 57 and 58 have been given full constitutional authority by the Eleventh General Assembly after being submitted to the Presbyteries and receiving the necessary two-thirds (2/3) approval of the Presbyteries,” and Whereas, BCO 56-5 states, regarding the questions a minister is to ask when doing an infant baptism, “The minister shall then propose the following questions. . .”, and Whereas, the word “shall” requires the minister to use the specific wording of the questions as recorded in BCO 56-5, and Whereas, in BCO 56-5, question three contains the archaic phrase “o f God’s appointment”, Therefore, be it so ordered that the BCO be revised by the following action: Delete the phrase “o f God’s appointment” and add the phrase “appointed by God” in BCO 56-5, so that question three will read, in part, . and that you will strive, by all the means appointed by God, to bring (him) up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord?” not adopted by the presbytery of new Jersey. [RAO 10-10] Attested by: /s/ James A. Smith, Stated Clerk 8. That OVERTURE 17 from Philadelphia Presbytery (“Add Vow for Elders when Receiving Members”) be answered in the negative. Adopted Grounds: such avow is already affirmed by the elders of the church (cf. BCO 21-5.7. -5 .8 ; 24-5.4).

“Add Vow for Elders when Receiving Members” Whereas, elders are called upon to shepherd the flocks that the Chief Shepherd has placed under their care (1 Peter 5:1-5), and Whereas, new church members come under the shepherding care and authority of the elders of the church that they join, and Whereas, new church members are called upon to assent their submission to “the government and discipline of the church” represented by the elder- shepherds of the church (BCO 57-5, Question 5), and Whereas, church membership represents not merely the commitment of the member to the authority of the church, but the commitment of the church to the care of new members; Therefore, we propose that the elders of the church express their commitment to shepherd their new members by adding this Question Six under BCO 57-5: 6. To the elders of the church (standing): Do you, as elders and shepherds of this congregation, commit yourselves to provide spiritual care, nurture, and discipline to these who have submitted themselves to your God-given authority, recognizing that they are now among the sheep for whom you will give an account to the Chief Shepherd? Adopted November 13, 1999, by the presbytery of philadelphia for presentation to the 28th General Assembly, 2000, in Tampa, Florida Attested by: /s/ Frank D Moser, Stated Clerk 9. That OVERTURE 18 from Ellisville PCA, Ellisville, MS (“Amend BCO 13-1 to Allow Additional Ruling Elders as Presbytery Commissioners”) be answered in the negative Adopted Grounds: the problem of limited ruling elder participation does not appear to be a function of the standards established in the BCO, and thus is not remedied by the proposed expansion.

source: OVERTURE 18 From Ellisville PCA, Ellisville, MS
body: “Amend BCO 13-1 to Allow Additional Ruling Elders as Presbytery Commissioners” Whereas, the formation of the Presbyterian Church in America was the result of the Lord, in His Providence, convicting elders of the need to remain true to the Biblical principles and teachings upon which our faith is based, and Whereas, our elder fathers in the faith were the first to point out and take a stand against errors being made and taught in the old Southern church, and Whereas, ruling elders have played an integral part in the organization and growth of the Presbyterian Church in America, serving diligently in all courts of the church, and Whereas, the parity of the elders hi pis compromised when the composition of church courts contain substantially more teaching elder commissioners than ruling elder commissioners, and Whereas, ruling elders serve the church generally, when called thereunto (BCO 8-3; Acts 20:28f), as well as the local congregation, and Whereas, the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America recognized the need for more ruling elder involvement and participation in said court by amending the Book of Church Order to increase the number of ruling elder commissioners from each church from one ( 1) to two (2), with additional commissioners for larger congregations, and Whereas, there is a similar need for more ruling elder involvement and participation in the church presbyteries. Now Therefore, Be it Resolved, that the undersigned Session overtures the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to amend the Book of Church Order, 13-1, to increase the number of ruling elder commissioners to presbytery meetings from each church from one ( 1) to two (2), with additional commissioners for larger congregations, and Be it Further Resolved, that the Book of Church Order 13-1 be amended by deleting the present paragraphs and substituting the following, to wit: the presbytery consists of all the teaching elders and churches within its bounds that have been accepted by the Presbytery. When the Presbytery meets as a court it shall comprise all teaching elders and ruling elders as elected by their Session. Each congregation is entitled to two ruling elder representatives for the first 350 communing members or fraction thereof, and one additional ruling elder for each additional 500 communing members or fraction thereof. Adopted by the Session of the undersigned Session at a called meeting on the 5th day of December, 1999. Attested by: Is/ Charles Probst, clerk of Session, Ellisville Presbyterian Church NOTE: This Overture was rejected by Grace Presbytery (RAO 10-10) 10. That OVERTURE 6 from Cherokee Presbyterian Church (“Amend BCO 16-4 to Allow that Exceptions May Not Be Taught”) be answered in the negative. Adopted grounds the powers of the presbytery with respect to this issue are well defined in the Constitution (e.g., BCO 13-9.d, -9,f.) and have been carefully and consistently construed by the General Assembly in judicial cases (e.g., M14GA, pp. 125-126, M18GA, p. 205, M20GA, pp. 163-164). Further, the proposed amendment introduces, without definition, terminology unknown to our Constitution, and thus liable to misinterpretation.

“Amend BCO 16-4 to Allow that Exceptions May Not Be Taught” the session of the cherokee presbyterian church respectfully requests that the North Georgia Presbytery nevertheless forward for consideration by the PCA ’s General Assembly in June, 2000, the following overture (to be accompanied by notice of the Presbytery’s negative vote on the overture at its fall meeting): We hereby request the 2000 General Assembly of the PCA proceed with the process to add to the BCO, Chapter 16 on Church Orders the following Paragraph 16-4: “When the process of examination reveals any exceptions to the constitutional standards that the relevant court judges, if taught, to be harmful to the peace and well-being of the church (though not serious enough to disqualify the candidate for office), it may by a majority vote direct the candidate for office not to teach the exception.” Rationale: this clarifies by making explicit to all what is understood by many to bean implicit power of the courts of the church. thank you for your consideration of this request. Letter dated January 7, 2000 and signed by Rev. Ted Lester, Moderator, for the session of cherokee presbyterian church of Woodstock, Georgia. NOTE: North Georgia Presbytery had previously rendered a negative vote upon its earlier consideration. at the last meeting of the presbytery of north Georgia, on January 15, 2000, the Committee on Bills and Overtures in their report, instructed the clerk to forward this overture to the office of the stated Clerk, Presbyterian Church in America, for handling. 11. That OVERTURE 13 from Susquehanna Valley Presbytery (“Re-Ordination of Former PCA Ministers”) be answered in the negative Adopted Grounds: The procedure, if desired, is already available to the Presbytery via the “extraordinary” clause of BCO 21-4. NOTE: the premise of the first “Whereas” is not well founded. A presbytery may do as Potomac Presbytery in such cases, e.g., adopt a resolution as follows: “That, upon review as required by BCO 13-2 and 34-10, and finding no culpable dereliction, nor evident lack of acceptance by the church, the following Teaching Elders be continued on the roll w/o call: — — ----------. This continuance is approved with the understanding that it shall be reviewed annually, and with the understanding that each candidate shall have the responsibility to demonstrate that a continued absence of call is not the result of “breach of his covenant engagement”, or “lack of acceptance to the church” (cf. b pp ,.A.2.i.).”

“Re-ordination of former PCA Ministers” whereas the Book of Church Order rightly calls fora presbytery to divest a minister if he continues on the rolls without call for over three years (BCO 34-10, 13-2), and Whereas, this procedure is rarely followed, and Whereas, this leads to men not being as closely connected to sessions as is good for them or as is good for the work of the church, and Whereas, this often puts pressure on presbyteries to approve “calls” which are questionable, and Whereas, one reason for this failure of presbyteries to act is that both the man and his presbytery are hoping a call will come and if it does after he is divested he would have to go through the entire ordination process again, Therefore, the Presbytery of Susquehanna Valley hereby overtures the General Assembly to add a new section 5 as follows to chapter 21 of the BCO and renumber the following sections: NEW 21-5: Modified procedures may be used for the re-ordination of a former PCA minister who receives a call to a particular church after he was divested without censure at his request (38-2) or was divested of his office without censure against his will (34-10). The presbytery in which he is being called shall carefully investigate the circumstances under which he was divested. If the presbytery decides that the reason he was divested was simply a lack of call, it may proceed to give him the trials for ordination outlined in 21-4 without going through the normal candidate, licensure, and internship procedures. At its discretion, the presbytery may accept his previous ordination in lieu of examining him in the Greek, and Hebrew languages, church history, and the history of the PCA. Adopted by the Presbytery of Susquehanna Valley on February 18, 2000. Attested by: /s/ David F. Rundle, Stated Clerk 12. That OVERTURE 4 from James River Presbytery (“Clarify Use of Professional in Cases of Process”) be answered in the affirmative with the following substitute. That BCO 32-19 be amended by deleting the current language (indicated by strikeouts) and replacing it with the following new language. 32-19. No professional counsel shall be permitted as such to appear and plead in cases of process in any court; but an accused person may, if he desires it, be represented before the Session by any communing member of the same particular church, or before any other court, by any member of that court. A member of the court so employed shall not be allowed to sit in judgment in the case. 32-19. The accused shall be entitled to be represented before the courts of this church by counsel, who shall have the right to be heard by oral and/or written argument. Any such counsel shall be a communing member of the Presbyterian Church in America. Any member of a court so engaged shall not be allowed to sit in judgment of the case. No person shall accept any fee or other remuneration for any service rendered as counsel, but reimbursement may be made to cover any personal expenses incurred or to be incurred by such counsel in the course of representation. Adopted Grounds: The overture identifies important defects in the provision as it stands, i.e., the possibility of discontinuity of counsel in the appeals process, and the uncertainty of the church with respect to the meaning of “professional counsel”. The substitute language provides improved economy, consistency, and logical progression in the proposed amendment, while making plain the otherwise implied rights of counsel, and broadening the membership criteria for counsel.

“Clarify use of professional counsel in cases of Process” Whereas, BCO 32-19 forbids the use of professional counsel “as such” in cases of process but permits an accused to be represented before the session of the church of the accused by a member of that church, and before any other court by a member of that court; and Whereas, the phrase “as such” is subject to different interpretations; and Whereas, the limitation on representation before a court higher than the Session may destroy the continuity of representation of the accused and otherwise prejudice his defense, Therefore, Be it Resolved that the James River Presbytery respectfully overtures the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to clarify, amend, and restate BCO 32-19 so that it will read in its entirety as follows: 32-19 An accused person may be counseled and represented before the Session or any other court by any communing member of the same particular church of which the accused is a member, or by any member o for commissioner to a court before which the accused appears, provided, however, that the individual serving as counsel may not serve for a fee or other remuneration Notwithstanding the foregoing, payments may be made to reimburse or cover any direct expenses incurred or to be incurred by such counsel in the course of representation. If such counsel is a member o for commissioner to the court before which the accused appears, he may not sit in judgment in the case. adopted at the spring stated meeting of james river presbytery on april 8, 2000. Attested by: /s/ Eugene H. Friedline, Stated Clerk 13. That OVERTURE 7 and COMMUNICATION 1 from North Florida Presbytery (“Decry contentious practices of the “Presbyterian and Reformed News”) be answered in the negative. Adopted Grounds: The Overture would improperly have the Assembly conclude as grounds for the requested action censurable offenses without due process, or would restrain improperly and unwisely dissemination of information in the Church. Further the Overture appears to unwisely call into question the supreme value of an independent press to a church whose authority is grounded in the willing compliance of an informed conscience and whose testimony to the truth is, humanly speaking, enabled by full and free debate. The overture appears to neglect entirely the essential place such an independent press has had in the history of the conservative movements in both northern and southern Presbyterian Churches, and the similar language of condemnation employed by those who found the views then expressed disagreeable. The wisest and most profitable response of presbyters to publications with which they disagree is to publish their own views, setting forth the truth, correcting errors, and evidencing both formally and materially the virtues that are rightly lauded in the Overture. Minority Report on OVERTURE 7 and COMMUNICATION 1 That Overture 7 and Communication 1 from the presbytery of north florida be answered as follows: The Presbyterian Church in America affirms that the only official publications authorized to record the story of the PCA are those sanctioned by the General Assembly. All other publications represent only the views and opinions of individuals within the denomination. Christian forbearance requires that these publications and the people responsible for them should be treated with the respect due to any minority view within the church. Moreover, we affirm the great value of an independent press in assuring full and free debate within the church and the role such publications have played in the history of the conservative movements in both the Northern and Southern Presbyterian Churches. The issues raised by the Overture from North Florida are serious, especially the allegations of possible violations of scripture and the subordinate standards However, the General Assembly is not the proper forum in which to investigate these reports. Consequently, the Assembly encourages the Presbytery of north florida to bring the charges to the courts of original jurisdiction to investigate and take whatever action is deemed appropriate. TE Craig Childs TE Stephen Estock TE Paul Frick TE Bill Lamkin RE Bill McClay TE Charles McGowan

source: OVERTURE 7 from presbytery of north florida
body: “Decry contentious practices of the ‘Presbyterian and Reformed News’” Whereas, the Presbyterian and Reformed News, in an apparent disregard for the wisdom of Proverbs 6:16-19, [There are six things which the Lord hates, Yes, seven which are an abomination to Him: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that run rapidly to evil, a false witness who utters lies, and one who spreads strife among brothers, (NASB)] has printed stories and information that has created much confusion and fomented division within the PCA, and Whereas, the Presbyterian and Reformed News has printed statements even though the person or persons have asked not to be quoted (Spring 1998 issue, p. 5), and Whereas, the Presbyterian and Reformed News has printed statements about a member of North Florida Presbytery that called into question his reputation, integrity and Christian character (New Bulletin #27-1, June 14-15, 1999), and Whereas, the Presbyterian and Reformed News has printed summaries of the minutes of North Florida Presbytery, Therefore Be it Resolved, that the Presbytery of North Florida overtures the Presbytery of the Northeast to instruct the Editor(s) of the Presbyterian and Reformed News that Christian charity demands that they more seriously consider and humbly respect the requests of Christian brothers and Presbyteries. Ephesians 4:3 [I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, entreat you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling with which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, showing forbearance to one another in love, being diligent to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. (NASB)]. Moreover, in the light of wisdom of the Westminster Larger Catechism 144-145: Q. 144. What are the duties required in the ninth commandment? A. The duties required in the ninth commandment are, the preserving and promoting of truth between man and man, and the good name of our neighbor, as well as our own; appearing and standing for the truth; and from the heart, sincerely, freely, clearly, and fully, speaking the truth, and only the truth, in matters of judgment and justice, and in all other things whatsoever; a charitable esteem of our neighbors; loving desiring, and rejoicing in their good name; sorrowing for, and covering of their infirmities; freely acknowledging of their gifts and graces, defending their innocence; a ready receiving of a good report, and unwillingness to admit of an evil report, concerning them; discouraging tale-bearers, flatterers, and slanderers; love and care of our own good name, defending it when need requireth; keeping of lawful promises; studying and practicing of whatsoever things are true, honest, lovely, and of good report. Q. 145. What are the sins forbidden in the ninth commandment? A. The sins forbidden in the ninth commandment are, all prejudicing the truth, and the good name of our neighbors, as well as our own, especially in public judicature; giving false evidence, suborning false witnesses, wittingly appearing and pleading for an evil cause, out-facing and overbearing the truth; passing unjust sentence, calling evil good, and good evil; rewarding the wicked according to the work of the righteous, and the righteous according to the work of the wicked; forgery, concealing the truth, undue silence in a just cause, and holding our peace when iniquity calleth for either a reproof from ourselves, or complaint to others; speaking the truth unseasonably, or maliciously to a wrong end, or perverting it to a wrong meaning, or in doubtful or equivocal expressions; to the prejudice of truth or justice; speaking untruth, lying, slandering, backbiting, talebearing, whispering, scoffing, reviling, rash, harsh, and partial censuring; misconstructing intentions, words, and actions; flattering, vain-glorious boasting; thinking or speaking too highly or too meanly of ourselves or others; denying the gifts and graces of God; aggravating smaller faults; hiding, excusing, or extenuating of sins, when called to a free confession; unnecessary discovering of infirmities; raising false rumors, receiving and countenancing evil reports, and stopping our ears against just defense; evil suspicion; envying or grieving at the deserved credit of any, endeavoring or desiring to impair it, rejoicing in their disgrace and infamy; scornful contempt, fond admiration; breach of lawful promises; neglecting such things as are of good report, and practicing, or not avoiding ourselves, or not hindering what we can in others, such things as procure an ill name. The Presbyterian and Reformed News should more diligently strive to protect the good name and reputations of all people, even those who do not share the views of the Editor(s) and should promote the Biblical principles of mutual accountability, truthfulness and unity. Such a humble and gracious attitude is in accordance with, and even required by, the fifth membership vow: (BCO 57-5 – Do you submit yourselves to the government and discipline of the Church, and promise to study its purity and peace?) as well as the sixth ordination vow (BCO 21-5 and 24-5 – Do you promise to be zealous and faithful in maintaining the truth of the Gospel and the purity and peace of the Church, whatever persecution or opposition may arise unto you on that account? – Do you promise to strive for the purity, peace, unity and edification of the Church?), and Be it Further Resolved, that North Florida Presbytery decries the Presbyterian and Reformed News and states to all churches that we stand with and for our brother and fellow Teaching Elder and take exception to statements questioning a brother’s character made about our brothers in this Presbytery, and Be it Further Resolved, that the North Florida Presbytery instruct the Stated clerk of our presbytery to communicate with the Editor(s) of the Presbyterian and Reformed News that we do not want our minutes or summaries of the minutes of north florida presbytery printed in the Presbyterian and Reformed News, and Be it Further Resolved, that the presbytery of north florida forwards this overture to the 28th General Assembly as a communication to show our disfavor, dissatisfaction, and disapproval of much of the current contentious and divisive practices and faultfinding spirit of the Presbyterian and Reformed News, and Be it Further Resolved, that North Florida Presbytery overtures the General Assembly to decry much of the current contentious and divisive practices and faultfinding spirit of the presbyterian and reformed News, and Be it Finally Resolved, that the General Assembly instructs its Stated Clerk to include in his next letter to all teaching elders and clerks of Sessions, a statement about the view of the General Assembly regarding the Presbyterian and Reformed News. approved by the presbytery of north florida this day: January 14, 2000. Attested by: /s / Randy L. Wilding, Stated Clerk

“Improper Dissemination of Information Regarding Judicial Cases and Information Detrimental to Reputations” Whereas, the Lord, through the Apostle Paul, urges believers to live “with all humility and gentleness, with patience, showing forbearance to one another in love, being diligent to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:2-3 – NASB); and Whereas, the authors of the Westminster Larger Catechism explain that the Ninth Commandment requires of us “the preserving and promoting of truth between man and man, and the good name of our neighbor, as well as our own;…a charitable esteem of our neighbors; loving, desiring, and rejoicing in their good name; sorrowing for, and covering of their infirmities;…a ready receiving of a good report, and unwillingness to admit of an evil report, concerning them;” (WLC 144); and Whereas, the Book of Church Order (PCA) in 27-1 says, “Discipline is the exercise of authority given the Church by the Lord Jesus to instruct and guide its members and to promote it’s purity and welfare”; and Whereas, the Book of Church Order (PCA) 27-5 says, “Scripture law is the basis of all discipline because it is the revelation of God’s Holy will. Proper disciplinary principles are set forth in the Scriptures and must be followed. They are: - **a.** Instruction in the Word; - **b.** Individual’s responsibility to admonish one another; - **c.** If the admonition is rejected, then the calling of one or more witnesses; - **d.** If rejection persists, then the Church must act through her court unto admonition, suspension, excommunication and deposition. Steps (a) through (d) must be followed in proper order for the exercise of discipline”; and Whereas, the Presbyterian and Reformed News which is published primarily by members of the PCA has printed articles about judicial cases which are in process and therefore it circumvents the constitutionally ordained church courts, and may prejudice the court by the information it disseminates; Therefore Be it Resolved, that Southeast Alabama Presbytery overture the General Assembly to instruct all members of the Presbyterian Church in America not to publish information about a judicial case which is in process; and Be it Further Resolved, that General Assembly instruct all members of the Presbyterian Church in America to follow the procedures set down in the Book of Church Order when there is a grievance and to refrain from improperly disseminating information detrimental to the reputation of others, and Be it Finally Resolved, that the General Assembly instruct its Stated Clerk to include in his next pastoral letter to all churches in the PCA a copy of this overture. adopted unanimously by the presbytery of southeast Alabama, April 28, 2000, at Millbrook, Alabama. Attested by: Is/ Henry Lewis Smith, Stated Clerk 15. That OVERTURE 5 from Louisiana Presbytery (“Amend BCO 38-4 by Deletion”) be answered in the negative. Adopted Grounds: The third and fourth “Whereas” clauses misconstrue the proper interpretation of the provision in question. Rightly construed, no remedy is needed. It cannot be “reasonably inferred that administrative removal from the membership roll may NOT occur under this provision if the member were regularly worshipping and participating in another church other than the one in which he took his membership vows” because the sentence is qualified by the opening sentence: “When a member of a particular church has willfully neglected the church fora period of one year, or has made it known that he has no intention of fulfilling the church vows. . . Clearly mere participation at another church does not exempt one from consideration under this standard. The provision is further qualified in the second paragraph by the phrase “will not fulfill his membership obligations” (emphasis added) which obligations are summarized in the parenthetical in the first paragraph, i.e., “(BCO 57-5, nos. 3- 5)” . Again, clearly mere participation in another church does not satisfy this standard. On the other hand, the sentence in question (“in this or any other branch of the visible Church”) is important to keep in the provision because it makes clear that if a person is willing to fulfill the vows of membership (not just attend or participate) in another church, the Session should not remove the person from the roll in an act of “pastoral discipline”, but dismiss the person to that branch of the visible Church.

“Amend BCO 38-4 by Deletion” Whereas, BCO 38-4 creates a method for administrative removal of a member from the church of the lord jesus christ without formal judicial process under certain specified circumstances. Whereas, the first sentence of the second paragraph of BCO 38-4 reads thusly: “If after diligently pursuing such pastoral discipline, and after further inquiry and due delay, the session is of the judgment that the member will not fulfill his membership obligations in this or any other branch of the visible church (cf. BCO 2-2), then the Session shall erase his name from the roll.” Whereas, the highlighted words create serious constitutional problems for a Session faithfully attempting to exercise its duties under BCO 38-4, inasmuch as it might be reasonably inferred that administrative removal from the membership roll may NOT occur under this provision if the member were regularly worshipping and participating in another church other than the one in which he took his membership vows. Whereas, the highlighted words may be reasonably interpreted to require a Session to exercise formal discipline rather than administrative removal, if a member ignored his membership vows and began attending another congregation. Whereas, it is the intent of scripture and our constitutional standards that decisions pertaining to the election of officers and well-being of particular congregations should be decided by those members who are faithful to their membership vows. Whereas, the Session has the constitutional authority to receive, remove and dismiss members. BCO 12-5(a). Whereas, the Session should reasonably and equitably have the authority under BCO 38-4 without instituting formal process to administratively remove a member who has failed to keep his membership vows, regardless of whether the member is attending another congregation. Therefore, Be it Resolved that Louisiana Presbytery respectfully moves that the first sentence of the second paragraph of BCO 38-4 be amended to delete the highlighted language above so that the sentence will read thusly: “If after diligently pursuing such pastoral discipline, and after further inquiry and due delay, the session is of the judgment that the member will not fulfill his membership obligations, then the Session shall erase his name from the roll.” Presbytery respectfully requests that the 28th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America concur in this proposed amendment and that there be the initiation of constitutional amendment procedures in accordance with our Book of Church Order. Adopted by Louisiana Presbytery on October 16, 1999. Attested by: /s/ George Thompson, Stated Clerk 16. That OVERTURE 27 from Gulf Coast Presbytery (“Amend RAO 14-7-3 by Adding Another Sentence”) be answered in the negative. Adopted Grounds: A rule change adopted so recently by the Assembly ought not to be reviewed again until the Church has had time to practically assess its effect. There is a presumptive virtue in settled law.

“Amend RAO 14-7-3 by Adding Another Sentence” WHEREAS, the purpose of the committee on review of presbytery records of the General Assembly is stated in RAO 14, and WHEREAS, the change in RAO 14-7-3 by last year’s General Assembly moves the committee on review of presbytery records away from its stated purpose by making it determine the theology and practice of the PCA, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that RAO 14-7-3 be amended to read as follows: 1. minutes approved with exception of substance which shall be presented to the General Assembly, which presentation include citation of any relevant Scriptural, Constitutional and /or RAO references and provide the Committee’s rationale for finding the exception of substance. The citation(s) and rationale are only to be seen as advice bv the General Assembly through her committee to help the Stated Clerk and the Presbytery cited to frame a satisfactory response to the citation. [Changes to current RAO underlined ] Reason: the committee on review of the presbytery records should not be in the business of framing doctrine and practice for the PCA. The committee’s work is to approve minutes and if exceptions of substance are found, to bring to General Assembly to vote on them. All references should be a help to a stated clerk and a presbytery to frame a satisfactory response to the next General Assembly. Heartland Presbytery Position Paper on Full Preterism Approved by presbytery action #99-71, 8/20/99 I. Definition of Full Preterism The terms “full preterism,” “consistent preterism,” “hyper-preterism,” “radical preterism,” and “Hymenaenism” have all been used with varying degrees of positive or negative connotations to define the same system of thought. A simple definition of a full preterist is a person who believes that all the prophecies of the Scripture have been fulfilled. Full preterism has at least the following characteristics: 1. A belief that the Second Coming of Christ has already occurred and no further bodily appearing is expected, 2. A belief that the resurrection has already happened and that therefore there will be no future physical resurrection of our present mortal bodies; 3. A belief that the final judgment of all men has already taken place (in 70 AD), the time when the separation of the goats and sheep (Matthew 25) took place, and that there is to be no future day of judgment for all mankind. Full preterism is truly a unique system of eschatology with a unique hermeneutical approach to many passages. Full preterists are not to be confused with those who teach a preteristic (fulfilled in the past) interpretation of some passages. All orthodox theologians have taken a preteristic interpretation of many prophetic passages (primarily those related to Christ’s first coming, but also to passages prophesying Christ’s judgment in 70 AD). In contrast to orthodoxy, full preterism teaches that all prophecy has been fulfilled. This paper is not an exposition of the system, but an elucidation of some of the key heretical teachings. II. body: It is the opinion of the CCB that Overtures 7, 20, 23, and 30 touch on issues that are not properly before the CCB since they do not seek constitutional amendment or constitutional advice. a. The Creation Study Committee Report has the status of any other study committee report, such as those on the gifts of the Holy Spirit and Freemasonry, that is, it is the thinking of a particular General Assembly on a specific subject. b. The Creation Study Committee Report, as with all other study committee reports adopted by a General Assembly, does not amend the constitution (BCO Preface, III. “The Constitution Defined” and BCO 26-1); only amendments effected by the proper constitutional procedures are actual and lawful amendments (BCO 26-2, 26-3 and 26-6). c. The Creation Study Committee Report has the status of being among those decisions of the General Assembly that are to be given “due and serious consideration by the Church and its lower courts when deliberating matters related to such actions” (BCO 14-7). d. Overtures relating to the Creation Study Committee Report would have the same status as the report, i.e. of being among those decisions of the General Assembly that are to be given “due and serious consideration by the Church and its lower courts when deliberating matters related to such actions” (BCO 14-7). e. It is the purview of the lower courts to determine the suitability of men applying for reception/ordination with regard to the men’s views on the matters raised in *in thesi* statements, subject always to proper review and/or judicial process. (BCO 13-6 and 13-9.a) (BCO 24-1) (BCO 11-3,4). Adopted by CCB

source: Presbytery of the Ascension to ask CCB to Examine the Minutes of the SJC
body: In response to the Overture from the Presbytery of the Ascension, the CCB understands the SJC to have acted in accord with GA’s directive to proceed according to the provisions of BCO 31-2 which required the SJC to enter an “investigation” phase of the matter before determining if there was sufficient evidence that “should result in raising a strong presumption of the guilt of the party involved” before instituting process and proceeding to trial. Presbyteries were informed by letter (dated August 29, 2000) of : (1) their right to submit evidence supporting their allegations to the SJC panel during this investigative phase; and (2) the time and place to submit evidentiary material related to the investigation. The understanding of the SJC was that further theological argument was appropriate for a trial, should an indictment have been rendered. Since no indictment was made, however, on the basis of the evidence presented by all notified parties it would have been inappropriate to try John Wood on the basis of theological arguments against matters neither he, nor the SJC, felt he supported. Had the matter moved to trial, it would have been proper for the presbyteries to make arguments for their allegations of theological error. The CCB acknowledges that, according to “Whereas #7-9” in Ascension Presbytery’s Overture, it is unfortunate that there was no formal, written response from the SJC to Ascension Presbytery’s inquiry following the panel’s initial contact and prior to its hearing. In order for presbyteries to feel that they have been adequately heard and fairly treated, it is vital that there be complete, timely and official responses to their inquiries. Adopted by CCB RE Neikirk requested that his negative vote be recorded and notified the committee that he may file a minority report. The chair appointed TE Chapell to respond for the Committee, if appropriate.

“Divide Heartland Presbytery” Whereas, the geographical boundaries of heartland presbytery are among the largest in the PCA; and, Whereas, the churches within the boundaries of iowa now number 6 organized churches numbering 813 members; two mission; and one possible church transferring from Independency; and, Whereas, stewardship of the local churches relates to time, talent and tithes; and, with the current distances, it is difficult to maintain close fellowship due to the travel time required; and, Whereas, requests from other Presbyteries with fewer churches and members have been approved (recognizing the same difficulties as Heartland); THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that Heartland Presbytery be divided so that the State of Iowa would become a separate Presbytery of the PCA effective January 1, 2002. Adopted at the 36th Stated Meeting of Heartland Presbytery, on November 11, 2000. Attested by: /s/ Lawrence N. Lunceford, Stated Clerk 10. source: OVERTURE 12 From Central Carolina Presbytery (to MNA)
body: “Divide Central Carolina Presbytery into Two Presbyteries” Whereas, the Central Carolina Presbytery exists for the Glory of God and the furtherance on His Kingdom here on Earth; Whereas, the Central Carolina Presbytery currently consists of Forty-Two (42) particular and mission congregations comprising more than Six Thousand (6,000) communing members within a geographical area requiring substantially more than three hours to cross; Whereas, the 16th General Assembly adopted guidelines for the multiplication of existing presbyteries into new presbyteries, which guidelines provide a set of ideals governing the development of new presbyteries; Whereas, pursuant to those guidelines, the Central Carolina Presbytery committed itself to a plan to grow into three separate presbyteries several years ago, which plan included developing three sub-regions (Metrolina, Triad, and Sandhills) within the presbytery and focusing church planting resources on developing new churches within each of these regions; Whereas, the Triad Region of the Central Carolina Presbytery has grown to Six (6) particular congregations and Two (2) mission congregations comprising more than One Thousand communing members and these churches have developed a strong sense of mutual care and potential for shared ministry and joint ministry projects; Whereas, Five of the particular congregations located in the Triad Region have communing membership in excess of One Hundred Twenty-Five, with strong prospects for continued growth in the future; Whereas, there is a commonly recognized regional identity within the Eleven (11) County area known as the "Piedmont Triad" in North Carolina which the Triad Region of Central Carolina Presbytery was formed to build upon and which does not partition any existing metropolitan areas; Whereas, the Central Carolina Presbytery believes it is consistent with the guidelines of the 16th General Assembly to form a new presbytery in the Eleven County area of North Carolina known as the "Piedmont Triad" and that this multiplication of ministry would further the advance of God's Kingdom and the growth of His Church on Earth; NOW, THEREFORE the Central Carolina Presbytery hereby petitions and overtures the General Assembly pursuant to 14-6(e) of the Book of Church Order of the Presbyterian Church in America as follows: (1) To remove the Eleven County area commonly known as the "Piedmont Triad" of North Carolina and consisting of Surry, Yadkin, Davie, Davidson, Stokes, Forsyth, Rockingham, Guilford, Randolph, Caswell and Alamance Counties from the existing bounds of the Central Carolina Presbytery; (2) To erect the "Piedmont Triad Presbytery of North Carolina," establishing the boundaries of such presbytery to include those Eleven counties and the particular and mission congregations currently located within them; (3) To authorize the conduct of business by this newly established church court effective July 1,2001, consistent with Chapter 13 of the Book of Church Order and such other provisions as may apply. It is so moved and approved by the Assembled Court of the Central Carolina Presbytery this 27th day of January, 2001. Attested by: /s/ Howie Burkhalter, Moderator, Central Carolina Presbytery This Overture was moved, seconded and approved at a duly constituted meeting of the Central Carolina Presbytery at which a quorum was present. Attested by: /s/ David M. Frierson, Stated Clerk 11. source: OVERTURE 22 from Great Lakes Presbytery (to MNA)
body: "Divide Great Lakes Presbytery and Form Ohio Valley Presbytery" Now Therefore, Be it Resolved, that Great Lakes Presbytery unanimously overtures the 29th General Assembly to form a new “Ohio Valley” Presbytery by: Establishing the boundary of the continuing Great Lakes Presbytery to include: All the state of Michigan; All of Indiana north and east of and including the counties of Porter, Jasper, Pulaski, Fulton, Wabash, Huntington, Wells, and Adams; and All of Ohio currently in Great Lakes Presbytery north and east of and including the counties of Mercer, Shelby, Logan, Union, Madison, Pickaway, Hocking, Vinton, and Meigs. Establishing the boundary of the new Ohio Valley Presbytery to include: All of Indiana that is currently in the Great Lakes Presbytery and is south and west of but not including the counties of Porter, Jasper, Pulaski, Fulton, Wabash, Huntington, Wells, and Adams; and All of Ohio south and west of but not including the counties of Mercer, Shelby, Logan, Union, Madison, Pickaway, Hocking, Vinton and Meigs. All of the counties of Kentucky currently in Great Lakes Presbytery. This action is to be effective July 1, 2001. Adopted unanimously at the Stated Meeting of the Great Lakes Presbytery held on October 13, 2000 12. That the General Assembly approve the 2002 budget of Reformed University Ministries, and note the budget including the affiliated campus ministries is provided to the General Assembly for its information; and further, that the Assembly note with thanksgiving the opportunities and challenges represented by the entire 2002 budget. Deferred to the AC Report, p. 254-255 13. That the General Assembly re-elect TE Kennedy Smartt to another term and elect TE D. Charles (Chuck) Frost to the Presbyterian and Reformed Joint Commission on Chaplains and Military Personnel (PRJC) as members of the Class of 2005. Adopted 14. That the General Assembly adopt the 2002 GA/MNA budget and commend it to the churches for their support. Deferred to the AC Report, p. 254-255 15. That the General Assembly pause now for a 15 minute season of prayer for the advancement of the Gospel in North America – praying for the following “renewed commitments”: - A renewed realization that the church is built by our Lord; - A renewed commitment to prayer; - A renewed commitment to unity in the church; - A renewed commitment to reaching the many cultures, ethnic/racial groups and socio-economic groups in North America; - A renewed commitment to mercy ministries – preaching the Gospel in Word and showing the mercies of Christ in deed; - A renewed commitment to the kind of stewardship of the Lord’s resources that will give greater priority to the advancement of the Gospel; - A greater commitment to functional teamwork. Adopted 16. That the General Assembly call upon our presbyteries to set aside a significant portion of their meetings to pray for the advancement of Gospel through the revitalization of our existing churches and through the planting of new churches – throughout North America and throughout the world. Adopted 17. That the General Assembly encourage each congregation and presbytery of the General Assembly to seek with a greater zeal the Lord’s calling for them in the advancement of the Gospel. I Corinthians 12:7 and Ephesians 4:7 promise that the Spirit of God has given each a gift for the common good and the building of the church. Just as there is a calling to every local church in reaching the local community and the world with the Gospel, so there is a calling for every congregation in church planting – reaching our “Judea and Samaria,” as well as our “Jerusalem” and the “uttermost parts.” Adopted 18.
