source: OVERTURE 26 From New York State Presbytery (to MNA)
body: “Redraw New York State and Ascension Presbytery Boundaries” Whereas, the current western boundary of the New York State Presbytery includes central New York east and including Wayne, Ontario and Steuben counties; and, Whereas, the current eastern boundary of the Ascension Presbytery includes western New York west and including Monroe, Livingston and Allegany counties; and Whereas, the city of Rochester located in Monroe County and within the boundary of Ascension Presbytery has no PCA church; and Whereas, there are several families who have expressed interest in the past several years in forming a core group for the purpose of starting a PCA church in the Rochester area; and Whereas, there are some families who travel from the Rochester area to New Life Presbyterian Church in Ithaca, NY, a mission church in the New York State Presbytery, for worship; and Whereas, these same families have indicated a desire to affiliate with the New York State Presbytery; and Whereas, the New York State Presbytery would like to initiate and oversee this developing PCA work in the Rochester area as part of its vision to plant healthy and reproducing PCA churches in every major city in upstate New York; Therefore, Be It Resolved that the New York State Presbytery hereby overtures the 29th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to redraw the western boundary of New York State Presbytery and the northeastern New York boundary of Ascension Presbytery, to wit, that the counties east of and including Monroe and Livingston be transferred to New York State Presbytery, and furthermore, that the counties east of and including Steuben remain with the New York State Presbytery, to be effective July 1, 2001. Adopted by New York State Presbytery on January 20, 2001. Attested by: /s/ James Stewart, Stated Clerk COMMUNICATION 6 From Ascension Presbytery (to MNA) “Ascension Presbytery Concurs with New York State Presbytery’s Request” Dear Dr. Taylor, This letter is to inform you that the Presbytery of the Ascension, at its Stated Meeting on April 27-28, 2001, voted to concur with Overture 26 from New York State Presbytery; thus agreeing that the New York counties of Monroe and Livingston should be transferred from the Presbytery of the Ascension to the New York State Presbytery. Sincerely in Christ, /s/ Frederick R. Neikirk, Stated Clerk 19. That Overture 29 From TE Andrew Lee of Northern California Presbytery be answered in the negative on the following grounds: 1. Regarding Items 1-4, the overture presents no reasons for requesting this review. There is no self-evident rationale for requiring this review. There are no allegations of impropriety or misuse of funds. Therefore, even the overture itself presents no reasons to proceed with an action that would require a significant expenditure of staff time. 2. Item 4 calls for an adjustment of 1990 - 1997 church planting budgets, based on a standard put in place in 1997. It is not common practice to apply a new standard to previous actions in matters such as this, and there is no rationale offered for doing so in this case. 3. This overture and its requested actions were not supported by Northern California Presbytery, the court to which they were originally presented. 4. Effective January 1, 2000, MNA discontinued the practice of assessing fees on project funds. Since that date, it has been the practice to apply 100% of every designated dollar to the project for which it is designated. 5. Regarding membership in ECFA, the MNA Committee believes that current accountability structures are sufficient to sustain the credibility of the ministry. Its annual audit by an independent accounting firm is reviewed by the MNA Committee and the General Assembly. All aspects of MNA's work are subject to the review of the General Assembly annually. MNA believes that any value gained from ECFA accreditation is more than offset by the time and expense required to maintain such accreditation. Adopted

source: OVERTURE 29 From TE Andrew Lee of Northern California Presbytery
body: “Direct MNA to Report Administrative Fees” Whereas, in October 1997 the GA MNA Committee approved a policy: (a) to limit the maximum dollar amount (or percentage), of "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [project overhead/administrative fees] taken from funds raised for church planting projects; and (b) to disclose to select donors the existence and amounts of such costs as a percentage of donations; and Whereas, prior to October 1997, i.e., without aforementioned Committee-approved policy, GA MNA Staff prepared and administered church planting project budgets that included "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [project overhead/administrative fees]; and Whereas, GA MNA heretofore has not been a member of the Evangelical Council for Financial Accountability (ECFA; www.ecfa.org) as has another PCA Committee (Mission to the World) and PCA Agency (Covenant Theological Seminary) - organizations that are also involved in fundraising (Romans 12: 17b). (It should be noted that while GA MNA's financial records are audited annually by an independent firm, and all records are reviewed by normal General Assembly processes, ECFA membership is helpful both in terms of accountability and in increasing the confidence of donors); and Whereas, GA MNA as a Committee of the PCA is accountable to the General Assembly; Therefore, Be It Resolved that the General Assembly have GA MNA report to the General Assembly on the following: 1. Written policy and limits that GA MNA Staff used to determine "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [and/or similar overhead/administrative fees] in preparing and administering church planting project funds in the absence of the October 1997 Committee-approved policy; 2. Written policy and practices GA MNA Staff followed to disclose "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [and/or similar overhead/ administrative fees] to donors and church planters in the absence of the October 1997 Committee-approved policy; 3. "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [and/or similar overhead/administrative fees] in: (a) dollar amounts; (b) as a percentage of; donations (cf. guidelines in the October 1997 Committee policy); (c) timing as to when such fees were taken from church plant funds with respect to project's budget plan; and (d) the implicit cost of capital that "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [and/or similar overhead/administrative fees] imputed to each project when netted against funding covenants. Information for items 3(a) through 3(d) to be provided for all GA MNA project budgets not covered by the October 1997 Committee policy beginning from January 1990 through implementation of said Committee policy; 4. Recommended actions, if any, that should be taken for all projects in item #3 above if it is determined that "Field Assistance and Project Development Costs" [and/or similar overhead/administrative fees] were (a) lower relative to the guidelines set by the Committee's October 1997 policy; or (b) higher relative to the guidelines set by the Committee's October 1997 policy; and 5. GA MNA's current position regarding its membership in the ECFA. NOTE: This overture was presented to, and rejected by, Northern California Presbytery at the Spring 2000 Stated Meeting. Overture requested by TE Andrew Lee. Rejection recorded in meeting's minutes approved by Presbytery at the Fall 2000 Stated Meeting. Attested by: /s/ TE Andrew Lee 20. That Overture 32 from the Mid-America Presbytery be answered in the affirmative (see also Communication 1, page 173). Adopted

"J & R of Mid-America Presbytery into North Texas Presbytery" Whereas, Mid-America Presbytery, at times in its history having boundaries encompassing all of Oklahoma and parts of Kansas, Missouri, and Arkansas, and as many as ten churches, now, by the departure of churches and territory on several occasions to other expanding presbyteries, has been reduced to only part of the state of Oklahoma and to only four remaining churches with a combined communing membership of between four and five hundred, and Whereas, Mid-America Presbytery has the fewest churches of any of the contiguous PCA presbyteries, and Whereas, Mid-America Presbytery does not believe it currently has the resources of churches, presbyters, funds and morale most effectively to staff appropriately presbytery committees and commissions and move toward further growth, and Whereas, Mid-America Presbytery desires to gain encouragement towards future growth by being a part of a presbytery experiencing growth by church planting and the establishment of campus ministries, and Whereas, Oklahoma City and a corridor of counties connecting it to Texas are already part of North Texas Presbytery where currently, with the help of the Southwest Church Planting Network, two new Oklahoma City area church plants and a Reformed University Fellowship at the University of Oklahoma are being established, and Whereas, being received into North Texas Presbytery would immediately provide our churches with the option of participating in the three-presbytery, Southwest Church Planting Network (North Texas, South Texas and Southwest); and Whereas, our four remaining churches joining with North Texas Presbytery seems the best pathway for an eventual reestablishing of a larger Oklahoma area presbytery as soon as enough particular churches are formed, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Mid-America Presbytery – pending the consent of North Texas Presbytery to receive us – petitions the 29th General Assembly meeting in Dallas, Texas, in June, 2001, to be allowed to be joined and received, with our four particular churches, their officers and members of the presbytery, and all remaining Oklahoma counties into North Texas Presbytery, effective July 1, 2001, this action effectively dissolving Mid-America Presbytery. Adopted at the 40th Stated Meeting of Mid-America Presbytery, on April 20, 2001. Attested by: /s/ John Owen Butler, Stated Clerk COMMUNICATION 1 from North Texas Presbytery May 3, 2001 L. Roy Taylor, Stated Clerk RE: Mid-America Presbytery Overture to 29th GA to Join NTP Fathers and Brothers: At the 66th stated meeting of the North Texas Presbytery held April 27-28, 2001 at Park Cities Presbyterian Church, the Presbytery passed the following motion: “M&P that the North Texas Presbytery inform the 29th General Assembly that it concurs with the overture of Mid-America Presbytery to dissolve and to join the NTP.” This effectively places all Indian Territory within the boundary of the NTP. Yours in Christ, /s/ T. John Mulkey, Stated Clerk North Texas Presbytery 21. That Overture 34 from the Westminster Presbytery be answered to the affirmative. Adopted

*(to MNA)* “Revise Boundaries of Westminster Presbytery” Whereas, the counties of Pulaski and Carroll lie geographically in the New River Valley and at the extreme northeastern end of Westminster Presbytery, closer to all the churches in New River than to those in the entire southern cluster in Westminster; and Whereas, in the formative studies of potential boundaries for Westminster and New River Presbyteries, significant consideration was given to the possibility of our two Counties being assigned to New River; and Whereas, the geographical and cultural issues involving our two churches and those in New River Presbytery have led to very positive ministry and outreach sharing, particularly between the Virginia congregations of that Presbytery and ourselves; and Whereas, New River Presbytery has indicated a desire to receive those two Counties with a notation that adding our two Counties would strengthen their presbytery without unduly weakening a stronger Westminster; and Whereas, New River Presbytery has formed an ad-hoc committee to explore with some of the churches in James River Presbytery, and our two churches, the possibility of asking the General Assembly in the future to form a new Presbytery in the west-central area of Virginia; Now Therefore, be it resolved that Westminster Presbytery herewith overtures the 29th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to redraw the boundaries of Westminster and New River Presbyteries by transferring Pulaski County and that portion of Carroll County that lies east of Interstate 77 in the Commonwealth of Virginia, and the ministers and churches therein, from Westminster to New River Presbytery, effective September 30, 2001; and Be it further resolved that the Walthall-Wood Scholarship Fund assets be transferred to the New River Presbytery with the approval of this change of boundary since they are closely tied to the Draper’s Valley Presbyterian Church of Draper, Virginia. Adopted by Westminster Presbytery on April 21, 2001. Attested by: /s/ D. Steven Meyerhoff, Stated Clerk NOTE: New River Presbytery, acting in its 81st Stated Meeting on March 20, 2001, took the following action in regards to a proposed Overture of Westminster Presbytery requesting boundary changes: It was M/S/C to concur with that portion of a proposed overture by Westminster Presbytery dealing with the transfer of Pulaski and Carroll Counties in Virginia and/or the churches and Teaching Elders residing therein to New River Presbytery. Attested by: /s/ Don Clements, Stated Clerk 22. source: OVERTURE 36 From Central Carolina Presbytery (to MNA)
body: “North Hills PCA in Salisbury, NC, Seeking Admission into Newly-formed Triad Presbytery” Whereas, North Hills Presbyterian Church exists for the Glory of God and the furtherance of His Kingdom on Earth; Whereas, North Hills Presbyterian Church was admitted to the Central Carolina Presbytery in October of 1998 and has been blessed by its association with Central Carolina Presbytery and the Presbyterian Church in America; Whereas, North Hills Presbyterian Church is located in Rowan County, a county that adjoins the proposed boundaries of the Triad Presbytery; Whereas, North Hills Presbyterian Church lies in the extreme north of Rowan County next to the proposed boundary of the Triad Presbytery; Whereas, North Hills Presbyterian Church has a strong affinity to the Triad geographical region as well as to the churches in the new presbytery; Whereas, this proximity and affinity has already resulted in filial and ministry ties to the churches in the new presbytery; Whereas, official connection with the Triad Presbytery would strengthen North Hills Presbyterian Church, further its mission, and encourage its members to love and good deeds; Now Therefore North Hills Presbyterian Church hereby petitions and overtures the Central Carolina Presbytery and the General Assembly that it be allowed to join the newly-formed Triad Presbytery outside its geographical bounds effective July 1, 2001. Adopted by the Moderator of Session, North Hills Presbyterian Church and the Clerk of Session, North Hills Presbyterian Church /s/ Jerry C. Currin, Moderator and /s/ M. J. Smith, III, Clerk of Session 23. That Overture 37 from the Potomac Presbytery be answered in the affirmative. *Adopted*

“Erect New Presbytery” westminster presbytery hereby notifies the General Assembly of its intention to withdraw from the Presbyterian Church in America, effective at the January 2002 stated meeting of Presbytery; and the General Assembly be overtured to take the following action: That the General Assembly, under the powers granted to it under the PCA Constitution to erect new presbyteries and to unite and divide presbyteries per their request, hereby established a new presbytery, in accordance with the following criteria: those churches and ministers which have certified to the stated clerk of Westminster Presbytery by the January 2002 stated meeting of said presbytery that they wish to remain in Westminster Presbytery, shall be constituted as Westminster Presbytery; while those churches and ministers which have not certified to the stated clerk of westminster presbytery by the january 2002 stated meeting of said presbytery that they wish to remain in westminster Presbytery, shall be constituted as a new Presbytery, effective that date, with the same boundaries as the present Westminster Presbytery. Adopted by Westminster Presbytery on May 15, 2001. Attested by: Is/ D. Steven Meyerhoff, Stated Clerk 25. that communication 5 from the Westminster Presbytery be received by the 29th General Assembly as supporting information to overture 38, and that, in order to honor the original conditions under which Westminster Presbytery joined the PCA, the communication be spread upon the minutes of the 29th General Assembly. the committees response to Recommendation 24 above answers Communication #5 in Recommendation 25. communication 5 From Westminster Presbytery (to MNA) “Erect New' Presbytery” Dear Dr. Taylor, May 16, 2001 a ta called meeting of westminster presbytery on may 15, 2001, the Presbytery took action to withdraw from the Presbyterian Church in America, effective at its January Stated Meeting, and to overture the PCA General Assembly to recognize this fact and constitute a new Presbytery, with the same geographic boundaries, out of the teaching elders and churches that do not desire to leave the PCA. a copy of the Presbytery’s action is enclosed with this letter. Please consider the enclosed to be both a Communication and an Overture to the 29th General Assembly, informing and requesting action, on this matter. Also enclosed is a copy of the CCB advise to Westminster Presbytery, which we sought to follow in our action, and a copy of action taken by Westminster Presbytery and the General Assembly in 1974, reserving to Westminster Presbytery the right to withdraw from the PCA. We are exercising our right to withdraw in this action, but we are also seeking to be considerate of the current BCO and practices within the PCA. Please convey this material to the proper channels for action by the Assembly. Sincerely, in Christ, /s/ D. Steven Meyerhoff, Stated Clerk

source: OVERTURE 1 from Missouri Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: “Amend BCO 14-1(12), Increase Number on Committees, Extend Terms to Five Years” Whereas, the founders of our denomination, in order to minimize the concentration of power in the hierarchy of our denomination, created the structure of our General Assembly Committees and Agencies so that Committee members would be elected, in classes, for 4-year terms and are only eligible for re-election after a year has elapsed, Whereas, the responsibility and complexity of our Program Committees have grown as our denomination has grown, Whereas, it is very difficult for newly elected Committee members to function effectively until their 4-year term is almost half over, Whereas, this frequent turnover of Committee members coupled with the increased size and complexity of Committee operations tends to place more power in the hands of the permanent staff which is opposed to the intent of the founders of our denomination, Whereas, the proposed change provides for greater continuity in our Program Committees while still providing for the regular rotation of Committee members, Therefore Be it Resolved that BCO paragraph 14-1(12) in the second to the last paragraph be revised as follows: “Committee on Christian Education and Publications, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Ministries shall consist of fifteen (15) men divided into five classes of three men each, with two men being TEs and one RE or two men being REs and one TE on alternate years on odd years and four men each on even years, elected to serve five-year terms. Committees on Christian Education and Publications, Mission to North America, Mission to the World and Reformed University Ministries shall have one ruling elder and one teaching elder as alternates to fill any vacancy that may occur during the year.” Be it further resolved, that the first class of three (3) men to serve a five year term shall begin in 2003, should the 29th General Assembly approve this Overture, the consent of two-thirds (2/3) of the Presbyteries is given and the 30th General Assembly approves the same; and that each year thereafter there shall be an additional class of three (3) men who shall serve a five year term. Adopted by Missouri Presbytery on April 18, 2000. Attested by: /s/ David R. Stain, Stated Clerk 2. That Overture 2 from New Jersey Presbytery (“Amend BCO 58-5 – Use Unleavened Bread in Communion”) be answered in the negative. Grounds: There are no Scriptural grounds sufficient to mandate the exclusive use of unleavened bread in Communion. Adopted

source: OVERTURE 2 from New Jersey Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: “Amend BCO 58-5 – Use Unleavened Bread in Communion” Whereas, the first paragraph of *The Directory for the Worship of God*, states that “BCO 56, 57 and 58 have been given full constitutional authority by the Eleventh General Assembly after being submitted to the Presbyteries and receiving the necessary two-thirds (2/3) approval of the Presbyteries,” and Whereas, Exodus 12:8, 15-20 reveals that the Passover celebration and accompanying Feast of Unleavened Bread used unleavened bread, Whereas, Luke 22:1 reveals that the Lord Jesus, when He instituted the Lord’s Supper, was sharing a Passover meal with His disciples, and Whereas, 1 Corinthians 5:7 specifically states that believers are “unleavened” because Christ “our Passover” has been sacrificed, and Whereas, “leaven” is sometimes used in the Bible to denote sin, (cf. Matthew 16:6, 11-12), and Whereas, Jesus Christ is sinless, (Hebrews 4:15), Therefore, be it so ordered that the BCO 58-5 be revised by the insertion of the word “unleavened” before each occurrence of the word “bread” in the first, second, and fourth paragraphs and by adding these words at the end of the first paragraph: “If unleavened bread is unavailable, bread with leaven (yeast) may be used, but this is not to be the usual or normal practice of a congregation.” The first four paragraphs of BCO 58-5 shall now read (added words are underlined): “The table, on which the elements are placed, being decently covered, and furnished with *unleavened* bread and wine, and the communicants orderly and gravely sitting around it (or in their seats before it), the elders in a convenient place together, the minister should then set the elements apart by prayer and thanksgiving. *If unleavened bread is unavailable, bread with leaven (yeast) may be used, but this is not to be the usual or normal practice of a congregation.* The *unleavened* bread and wine being thus set apart by prayer and thanksgiving, the minister is to take the *unleavened* bread, and break it, in the view of the people saying: That the Lord Jesus Christ on the same night in which He was betrayed took bread; and when He had given thanks, He broke it, gave it to His disciples, as I, ministering in His name, give this bread to you, and said, “Take, eat; this is My body which is broken for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” Here the *unleavened* bread is to be distributed. After having given the *unleavened* bread, he shall take the cup, and say... Adopted by the Presbytery of New Jersey on May 20, 2000. Attested by: James A. Smith, Stated Clerk 3. That Overture 3 from Susquehanna Valley Presbytery (“Amend BCO 20-2 to Include Pastor in Search Committee for Assistant or Associate Pastor”) be answered in the negative. Grounds: There are many ways for a church to involve a senior pastor in the search process. It is not wise to mandate a specific BCO procedure regarding senior pastor involvement in calling an assistant or an associate pastor. Adopted

source: OVERTURE 3 from Susquehanna Valley Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: “Amend BCO 20-2 to Include Pastor in Search Committee for Assistant or Associate Pastor” Whereas, the *Book of Church Order* does not address the matter of searching for an assistant or associate pastor, and Whereas, for the peace and unity of the church it is vital that there be harmony among the pastoral staff of a church, and Whereas, any new assistant or associate pastor must be agreeable to and compatible with the senior pastor, Therefore be it resolved that the following be added to the BCO 20-2: “When a search committee for an associate pastor is formed by a congregation, the senior pastor shall automatically be a member of the committee. Before proposing a candidate to the congregation, the committee shall assure itself that the candidate is acceptable to and has the full support of the senior pastor. “In the case of a call to an assistant pastor, Session may act as the search committee or it may appoint church members as a search committee to bring a candidate for Session approval. In either case, the senior pastor shall be a member of the search committee.” Adopted by the Susquehanna Valley Presbytery on September 16, 2000. Attested by: D. F. Rundle, Stated Clerk 4. That Overture 4 be answered in the negative. Adopted as amended

source: OVERTURE 4 from Eastern Carolina Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: “Change Procedure for Pastoral Relationship Dissolution, BCO 23-1” Be it resolved that the Book of Church Order (BCO) 23-1 be amended as follows: **Existing provision**: BCO 23-1, first two paragraphs “BCO 23-1. When any minister shall tender the resignation of his pastoral charge to Presbytery, the Presbytery shall cite the church to appear by its commissioners, to show cause why the Presbytery should or should not accept the resignation. If the church fail to appear, or if its reasons for retaining its pastor be deemed insufficient, his resignation shall be accepted and the pastoral relation dissolved. If any church desires to be relieved of its pastor, a similar procedure shall be observed. But whether the minister or the church initiates proceedings for a dissolution of the relation, there shall always be a meeting of the congregation called and conducted in the same manner as the call of the pastor. In any case, the minister must not physically leave the field until the Presbytery or its commission empowered to handle uncontested requests for dissolution has dissolved the relation.” The **proposed revision** of the first two paragraphs only, follows: “BCO 23-1. When any minister shall tender the resignation of his pastoral charge to Presbytery, the Presbytery shall cite the church to appear by its commissioners, to show cause why the Presbytery should or should not accept the resignation. A meeting of the congregation shall be called and conducted in the same manner as the call of a pastor, and either accept the resignation or be prepared to show cause why the Presbytery should not accept it. If any church desires to be relieved of its pastor, a meeting of the congregation shall be called to request the Presbytery to dissolve the pastoral relation, and the meeting shall be conducted in the same manner as the call of a pastor. If the pastor is agreeable to the dissolution, he shall not leave the field until the Presbytery or its commissioners empowered to handle the congregation’s request has dissolved the relation. If the minister shall contest the requested dissolution, both the church and its pastor shall be cited to appear before the Presbytery to present their reasons for dissolution and reasons for contesting the dissolution. Since the bare fact that a majority of the members of a particular church desires to be relieved of its pastor is not per se a sufficient ground for dissolution, the Presbytery shall first hear from the church, then from the pastor in order to determine whether the dissolution is consistent with the Word of God in regard to the causes heard and would therefore be in the interest of both parties. In no case shall a contested request for dissolution be heard by a commission of Presbytery. **Supporting Reasons**: 1. This change in the BCO is needed to make clear that a movement for dissolution on the part of a pastor or a congregation must come in the form of a request to the Presbytery and, as such, it is to be carefully weighed in the light of all the circumstances. Dissolution of a pastoral bond is within the power of the Presbytery only and is not a “rubber stamp” action based solely on the will of either the congregation or its pastor. Especially in regard to congregational requests for dissolution, there is a growing sentiment within the PCA that the will of the majority of a congregation should prevail regardless of the issues that led to the request. In other words, a congregation, like a democracy, is entitled to be relieved of its pastor simply if a majority wishes it to be so, whatever the circumstances. Such a view may be congregational, but it is not Presbyterian. The majority of a congregation may have faulty, erroneous or unbiblical grounds for wishing the removal of its pastor, and in such cases the Presbytery may deny their request in favor of a minority in the congregation who wish to continue under the ministry of a faithful pastor. A majority of Israel wished to be relieved of Moses and return to Egypt, but they were clearly in error. Had a majority returned to Egypt, Moses no doubt would have continued to pastor the faithful minority and lead them on to the land of promise. A majority of the elders, and presumably the people, wished to be relieved of Jeremiah’s ministry and challenged his authority. “Thou speakest falsely: the Lord our God hath not sent thee...”(Jer. 43:2), they said; but our sympathy and support would have been with Jeremiah and the remnant who were faithful to his ministry. 2. A contested request of the congregation for dissolution of the pastoral bond is too weighty a matter to be handled by a commission of Presbytery. The Presbytery alone can authorize the formation of a pastoral bond, and the Presbytery alone should dissolve that bond. BCO 23-1 in its present form does not expressly grant Presbyteries authority to act through commissions in such serious matters although the language has been interpreted broadly. On the other hand, the present wording, “The minister must not leave the field until the Presbytery or its commission empowered to handle uncontested requests for dissolution has dissolved the relation”, could be said to suggest that only uncontested requests are appropriately handled by a commission. 3. There is need in the PCA to set in place a clear rule of discernment and judgment especially in matters of contested dissolution requests. To say that the majority of the congregation is entitled to its wish without regard to the circumstances and without evaluating the cause of the majority in the light of Scripture, is neither wise nor safe. To “save” a church by yielding to a majority in rejecting a faithful pastor without legitimate grounds may be to sacrifice a faithful minority to an unfaithful majority. This is not to save a church in the true sense of the word, for the blessing of God may be withdrawn from a church in such circumstances. If the congregation rejects one appointed by Christ to serve …

source: OVERTURE 7 From Calvary Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: "Require Exceptions for Views Other Than Six 24-Hour Creation Days" Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America is a confessional church based upon the Westminster Standards; and Whereas, our Confession of Faith states the time frame of God's original creative activity with the phrase, "in the space of six days" (WCF 4:1); and Whereas, growing historical evidence demonstrates the intent of the Westminster Assembly was to define the six creation days as 24-hour calendar days (At least 13 Westminster divines have been identified as attesting to a 24-hour creation day in their writings and recorded sermons; while none has been documented as holding to other time frames.); and Whereas, the official position of Calvary Presbytery states that the doctrine of the Confessional standards of the Presbyterian Church in America explicitly asserts that the world was created by divine fiat, literally “in the space of six days”. Because the Confession’s teaching on creation is unassailably grounded in Scripture, we joyfully proclaim that our preaching and teaching should conform to its content and emphases. (Adopted October 24, 1995); and Whereas, the 28th General Assembly affirmed that “...a diversity of views on creation days...is acceptable” thus, in essence, invalidating any definitive creedal statement; and Whereas, it has been our historic practice during elder examinations to note any differences from our standards as exceptions to be discussed by the church court; Therefore Be It Resolved, that the 29th General Assembly of the PCA declare that, with charity toward all our members, and with fidelity to the original authors of our confessional standards, and until evidence to the contrary is found, we understand the Westminster divines intended the phrase “in the space of six days” to specify that the six days of creation were days of normal duration with evening and morning; and Be It Further Resolved, that, for the peace of the church, any future candidates who differ with this original meaning should request an exception to the sense of the Confession unless documentation that the Westminster divines held other views is firmly established or unless the Standards are duly amended; and Be It Finally Resolved, that courts of original jurisdiction make these future determinations with care, charity, honesty, and impartiality. Adopted by Calvary Presbytery on January 27, 2001. Attested by: /s/ Charles E. Champion, Stated Clerk

source: OVERTURE 20 from New River Presbytery (to B&O & CCB)
body: “Allow Exceptions on Length of Creation Days” Whereas, the 28th General Assembly rejected the unanimous recommendation of the Creation Study Committee to wait two years before taking any action on the subject of the interpretation of the length of the days of creation in Genesis 1 and 2; and Whereas, the 28th General Assembly gave approval to an action which, while described by the Moderator as simply ‘pious advice’, is being perceived by many in the denomination as pressure to approve candidates for office without regard to their views on these issues, therefore, BE IT RESOLVED, that New River Presbytery, voting at its 80th Stated Meeting in Roanoke, Virginia on November 10, 2000, hereby encourages and requests the 29th General Assembly of the PCA to take the following actions as additions and further explanation of the Assembly’s response to the Creation Study Committee report: A. While the PCA recognizes both a historic and current diversity of views in the area of the length of creation days described in Genesis 1 and 2, it remains the primary and original responsibility of Presbyteries and Sessions to examine their candidates and determine if their views, no matter how diverse, are in accord with the Constitution of the church, and to determine if such views are exceptions. B. Presbyteries and Sessions who define any other view than the 24 hour day view as an exception to the standards in this area, in keeping with the actions of the 14th General Assembly, Section 143-52, Report of the Committee of Commissioners on Judicial Business, are to make the determination as to whether the teaching of these defined exceptions may or may not be allowed. C. Presbyteries and Sessions are counseled that, until such time as a view other than six, 24-hour solar day creation is adjudged to be out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine of the church through a change to the constitution, a final action in a judicial case, or the approval of a recommendation by a study committee, no officer should be refused ordination based on that exception alone. Adopted by New River Presbytery on November 10, 2000, at its 80th Stated Meeting. Attested by: /s/ Don K. Clements, Stated Clerk

source: OVERTURE 23 From Mississippi Valley Presbytery (to B&O &CCB) “Require Exceptions for Views Other than Six 24-Hour Creation Days”
body: Whereas, the Bible, in Genesis 1, Exodus 20:11, and Exodus 31:17 teaches that God created the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them in six days, and Whereas, our doctrinal standards (WCF 4, LC 15, and SC 9) affirm that it pleased God, by the word of his power, to create the world and all things in the space of six days, and all very good. Therefore, Be It Resolved, with charity toward all members and with fidelity to the original authors of our confessional standards, our understanding is that, unless evidence to the contrary is found, the Westminster Standards’ phrase “in the space of six days” means that the six days of creation were days of normal duration with evening and morning. Accordingly, for the peace of the church, any future candidates who differ with this original meaning should request an exception to the Confession, unless documentation that the Westminster Assembly meant otherwise is firmly established. We also pledge to make these future determinations, with care, charity, honesty and impartiality. adopted at the stated meeting of mississippi valley presbytery on february 6, 2001. Attested by: /s/R o ger G. Collins, Stated Clerk 6. that overture 30 from North Georgia Presbytery (“Affirm position of 28th assembly on diversity of views on creation Days”) be answered in the negative. Grounds: 1) it is the responsibility of the lower courts to examine and determine if a m an’s views are in accord with the constitution, not the man himself, not the General Assembly, except in cases of judicial process. 2) Using general revelation to determine doctrine is contrary to W CF 1.6. A dopted

source: overture 30 From North Georgia Presbytery (to B&O)
body: “Affirm position of 28th assembly on diversity of views on creation Days” Be it Resolved, that the North Georgia Presbytery overtures the 29th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to affirm the position of the 28th General Assembly, allowing a diversity of creation views, and likewise, with charity toward all our members, declare liberty-of-opinion concerning the intent of the westminster divines in their use of the phrase “in the space of six days.” be it further r esolved, that the 29th General Assembly recognizes that, within the church body, there are strongly held views concerning the days of creation; and. the Assembly acknowledges that for a creedal-based church, positions of diversity-of-view and liberty-of-opinion are not permanently satisfactory. Therefore, Presbyteries, Sessions and individual church members are encouraged to explore ways by which the scientific evidence of general revelation can be objectively studied and validated so that the church can move toward a unified understanding of how god created the universe and brought the earth into existence. Meanwhile, let us rejoice in our bonds of brotherhood and the hope we share in the reformed faith until our knowledge of his truth is more fully developed. Adopted by North Georgia Presbytery on April 17, 2001. Attested by: /s/ Dwight Allen, Stated Clerk that communication #4 from Western Carolina Presbytery be received as information, and spread upon the minutes of the 29th General Assembly. Grounds: We appreciate the concern and call for purity, peace, and unity in the denomination. A dopted COMMUNICATION #4 From Western Carolina Presbytery (to B&O) "A call for Purity, Peace and Unity of the Church" Fathers and Brethren: Two years ago, Western Carolina Presbytery initiated inquiry into the question of a woman preaching at the Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church of Tennessee Valley Presbytery, and also into the views of the Rev. John Wood on the subject of women preaching. Our concern, shared by many throughout the denomination, was that a woman should not be allowed to preach in a PCA pulpit. Tolerating false doctrine and false practice is one way in which other denominations have degenerated in the past. We believe that failing to express our concern would not have fostered the purity, peace and unity of our Church. It has been our wholehearted desire to encourage and promote the peace of the church. While we confess that we have been far from perfect in that quest, we believe that we can, with clear conscience, testify to the fact that we were earnest and sincere in all of our actions with regard to the John Wood matter. It was never our intention or desire that the Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church should leave the PCA. We wanted to know the facts. Our hope all along was for this congregation and its pastor to conform to the obvious teaching of Holy Scripture with regard to female preaching. With the events that have transpired since that time, and the departure of the Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church from the PCA, Western Carolina Presbytery desires to issue a call to the whole PCA to bring closure to this matter and to endeavor to pursue together both the purity, peace and unity of the Church. A Committee of Western Carolina Presbytery interviewed members of the Standing Judicial Commission regarding various reports that had been circulated and found that the investigative committee of the SJC found and reported that there were no discrepancies in the testimony of witnesses. Mr. Wood acknowledged that the testimony of the witnesses was accurate, and he stated before the panel "he should have been more careful to articulate his belief that women should not be ordained to the teaching or ruling eldership and that they should not be permitted to 'preach' in the traditional sense of authoritative teaching from the word of God, and teaching elders are called and ordained to do." Though one may differ with the finding of the SJC, the WCP Committee found that the SJC had a full and frank deliberation of the investigating panel's report and voted unanimously that "the investigation has not resulted in a strong resumption of guilt on the part of TE John Wood . . . and therefore judicial process should not be instituted against TE John Wood for his expressed views regarding women." We accept the decision of the SJC. The WCP investigation found that the SJC followed the Manual of Operations in determining to disqualify any one of the SJC members from participating in the deliberation. It is because of all the controversy and alleged irregularities surrounding the John Wood matter that we, once again, found ourselves duty-bound to raise the question of possible impropriety when reports were circulated that one or more members of the SJC had deliberately sought to protect John Wood at the Vision 2000 Caucus, but had not recused themselves from debating and voting. The WCP Committee investigated these allegations, and are happy to report that we have not been able to confirm them. In a statement made to two members of our Presbytery, RE John White, Chairman of the SJC, stated that he had not tried to advocate any particular course of action for the Assembly to take prior to the meeting of the Assembly itself. Mr. White indicated that at a meeting of the Vision 2000 Caucus several months prior to the 2000 General Assembly, he had set forth what he thought was the Constitutional position, viz., that the Assembly could not overturn the SJC's determination in the John Wood matter. We hereby report Mr. White's recounting of the facts, in the hope that the rumor that one or more SJC members have engaged in improper lobbying regarding the John Wood matter can now be put to rest. As we come to closure on the John Wood Judicial Matter, we hope and pray that all of us in the Presbyterian Church in America have learned from it. Perhaps the foremost lesson is that in order to maintain the bond peace (Ephesians 4:3-6) …

"Condemn Action of SJC in Judicial Matter 99-1 (re. TE John Wood)" Whereas, the 28th General Assembly instructed the SJC to hear from the Presbyteries concerned in the charges against John Wood; and Whereas, the SJC nor its panel of three men gave the Presbyteries an opportunity to speak to the theological and constitutional issues involved in the John Wood case; and Whereas, the SJC made theological interpretations without hearing from the Presbyteries; and Whereas, the SJC was instructed to determine Mr. Wood's views, in their report they do not focus on his views but that he has not agitated for the view that women may preach in the church; and Whereas, in the report of the panel there is a conflict between the testimony of Drs. Smith and Pipa and that of Mr. Wood with respect to Mr. Wood's definition of preaching and there was no opportunity for cross examination; and Whereas, there is a conflict between the report of Mr. Wood's position in the SJC ruling and his expressed position in his letter of October 2, 1999; and Whereas, such conflict can only be resolved through a trial with cross examination; and Whereas, in its spring meeting in 2000 the SJC would not allow its members who were from the Presbyteries that brought the original overtures to the SJC to vote on the issue, even though it was pointed out that in cases of original jurisdiction no member of the court was required to recuse himself. Therefore Be It Resolved, Calvary Presbytery overtures the 29th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to condemn the report of the 28th Assembly through the SJC (not to draw up charges against Mr. Wood and proceed to a trial). Adopted by Calvary Presbytery on January 27, 2001. Attested by: /s/ Charles E. Champion, Stated Clerk 9. That Overtures 9 and 11 from Evangel Presbytery (“Procedures on Assuming Original Jurisdiction”) be answered in the negative. Grounds: The concept of original jurisdiction is strong and dear to the denomination and must be preserved. However, the proposed changes to the BCO lead to the possibility of the court of original jurisdiction becoming the court of exclusive jurisdiction. The details of the proposed administrative procedures produce more difficulties than benefits in dealing with spiritual problems. Adopted

(to CCB & B&O) “Procedures on Assuming Original Jurisdiction Over Church Members” A New BCO 33-1 Process against all church members, other than ministers of the Gospel, shall be entered before the Session of the church to which such members belong, except in cases of appeal. This principle of original jurisdiction is designed to protect the right of the Session to investigate and adjudicate matters of sin within its bounds. Additionally, this principle of original jurisdiction is designed to protect the church member against judicial charges from those outside the Session who do not necessarily have access to the facts or access to the right of investigation. However, if there are other sessions in the same Presbytery which are not satisfied with how the Original Jurisdiction Session (OJS) has dealt with a matter of allegation against one of its members, then the following process shall be followed: 1. Those other sessions in the same Presbytery must formally request the OJS to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation of allegations against or reports surrounding this member within the OJS’s jurisdiction. 2. If the OJS conducts a BCO 31-2 investigation, then the matter will remain totally within the jurisdictional bounds of the OJS, subject, of course, to BCO provisions of complaint appeal, review and control. 3. If these other sessions in the same Presbytery (which followed step one above) do not believe that a BCO 31-2 investigation has taken place within a reasonable time period, these other sessions may request their Presbytery to assume original jurisdiction. 4. If at least two of these other sessions in the same Presbytery (who followed step one above) make such a request for their Presbytery to assume original jurisdiction, the matter shall be dealt with at the next stated meeting of the Presbytery at which time a commission will be appointed to conduct a preliminary hearing as to whether or not the OJS has conducted a BCO 31-2 investigation prior to the time of the commission's preliminary hearing. The commission may consider written briefs and oral presentations from the OJS and the two (or more) accusing sessions. The only question to be considered at this hearing is this: At the time of this commission's preliminary hearing, has the OJS conducted a *BCO 31-2* investigation of the alleged behavior or belief of its member. 5. If the commission determines that the OJS has conducted the *BCO 31-2* investigation, then the commission shall rule that the OJS has acted to exercise its right of original jurisdiction. 6. If the commission determines that the OJS has not conducted the *BCO 31-2* investigation (even though it has been properly asked to do so and has had sufficient time to do so), then the commission shall rule that the OJS has forfeited its right of original jurisdiction, shall rule that Presbytery has assumed the right of original jurisdiction and shall try the case as the court of original jurisdiction.

source: OVERTURE 13 From Central Carolina Presbytery (to CCB & B&O)
body: “Amend BCO 32-3 Regarding Sequence of Meetings of a Court in Judicial Process” Chapter 32 - General Provisions Applicable to all Cases of Process 32-3. It is appropriate that with each citation the moderator or clerk call the attention of the parties to the Rules of Discipline (BCO 27 through 46) and assist the parties to obtain access to them. When a charge is laid before the Session or Presbytery, it shall be reduced to writing and nothing shall be done at the first meeting of the court unless by consent of parties, except: 1. to appoint a prosecutor, 2. to order the indictment drawn and a copy, along with names of witnesses then known to support it, served on the accused, and 3. to cite all parties and their witnesses the accused to appear and be heard at another meeting which shall not be sooner than ten days after such citation. At the second meeting of the court, the charges shall be read to the accused, if present, and he shall be called upon to say whether he be guilty or not. If the accused confesses, the court may deal with him according to its discretion; if he plead and take issue, the trial shall proceed be scheduled and all parties and their witnesses cited to appear. The trial shall not be sooner than 14 days after such citation. Accused parties may plead in writing when they cannot be personally present. Parties necessarily absent should have counsel assigned to them. Rationale – Current wording explicitly mentions only two meetings of the court. The proposed change would result in three meetings in any full case of process – indictment meeting, arraignment, and trial. The current wording often results in unnecessary efforts. First, if the witnesses appear at the second meeting but the accused pleads guilty, then the witnesses appeared unnecessarily. Second, if the accused fails to appear, then the witnesses also appeared unnecessarily. Third, current wording implies that if the accused pleads not guilty, the trial could “proceed” at that second meeting. Thus, the prosecutor would need to completely prepare his case for the second meeting. However, if the accused pleads guilty the prosecutor would have fully prepared a case that he does not prosecute. On the other hand, if this second meeting is treated like an arraignment hearing, the problems go away. There would be no need to cite witness to appear at that meeting nor for the prosecutor to completely prepare the case prior to that meeting. If the accused pleads guilty at the second meeting (arraignment), the court can deal with him without ever needing to cite witnesses or to prepare a full prosecution. If he pleads not guilty at that meeting, then the witnesses will be cited to appear at the trial and the prosecutor can prepare his case in full, knowing there will be a trial. Adopted at the Winter Stated Meeting of Central Carolina Presbytery on January 26, 2001. Attested by: /s/ David Frierson, Stated Clerk
