source: OVERTURE 22 from Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (to OC)
body: “Urge Assembly to Adopt Overture 4 Regarding Nashville Statement” **Be it resolved that** Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery requests the 2019 PCA General Assembly to adopt Overture 4 from Calvary Presbytery: “Declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood’s ‘Nashville Statement’ on Biblical Sexuality as a Biblically Faithful Declaration" (Exhibit A, attached). _Adopted by Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery at its stated meeting,_ _February 23, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ RE Paul Rich, stated clerk_ **EXHIBIT A**

“Declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood’s ‘Nashville Statement’ on Biblical Sexuality as a Biblically Faithful Declaration” **Whereas** the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood’s "Nashville Statement" declares: **Article 1** WE AFFIRM that God has designed marriage to be a covenantal, sexual, procreative, lifelong union of one man and one woman, as husband and wife, and is meant to signify the covenant love between Christ and his bride the church. WE DENY that God has designed marriage to be a homosexual, polygamous, or polyamorous relationship. We also deny that marriage is a mere human contract rather than a covenant made before God. **Article 2** WE AFFIRM that God’s revealed will for all people is chastity outside of marriage and fidelity within marriage. WE DENY that any affections, desires, or commitments ever justify sexual intercourse before or outside marriage; nor do they justify any form of sexual immorality. **Article 3** WE AFFIRM that God created Adam and Eve, the first human beings, in his own image, equal before God as persons, and distinct as male and female. WE DENY that the divinely ordained differences between male and female render them unequal in dignity or worth. **Article 4** WE AFFIRM that divinely ordained differences between male and female reflect God’s original creation design and are meant for human good and human flourishing. WE DENY that such differences are a result of the Fall or are a tragedy to be overcome. **Article 5** WE AFFIRM that the differences between male and female reproductive structures are integral to God’s design for selfconception as male or female. WE DENY that physical anomalies or psychological conditions nullify the God-appointed link between biological sex and self-conception as male or female. **Article 6** WE AFFIRM that those born with a physical disorder of sex development are created in the image of God and have dignity and worth equal to all other image-bearers. They are acknowledged by our Lord Jesus in his words about “eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb.” With all others they are welcome as faithful followers of Jesus Christ and should embrace their biological sex insofar as it may be known. WE DENY that ambiguities related to a person’s biological sex render one incapable of living a fruitful life in joyful obedience to Christ. **Article 7** WE AFFIRM that self-conception as male or female should be defined by God’s holy purposes in creation and redemption as revealed in Scripture. WE DENY that adopting a homosexual or transgender selfconception is consistent with God’s holy purposes in creation and redemption. **Article 8** WE AFFIRM that people who experience sexual attraction for the same sex may live a rich and fruitful life pleasing to God through faith in Jesus Christ, as they, like all Christians, walk in purity of life. WE DENY that sexual attraction for the same sex is part of the natural goodness of God’s original creation, or that it puts a person outside the hope of the gospel. **Article 9** WE AFFIRM that sin distorts sexual desires by directing them away from the marriage covenant and toward sexual immorality— a distortion that includes both heterosexual and homosexual immorality. WE DENY that an enduring pattern of desire for sexual immorality justifies sexually immoral behavior. **Article 10** WE AFFIRM that it is sinful to approve of homosexual immorality or transgenderism and that such approval constitutes an essential departure from Christian faithfulness and witness. WE DENY that the approval of homosexual immorality or transgenderism is a matter of moral indifference about which otherwise faithful Christians should agree to disagree. **Article 11** WE AFFIRM our duty to speak the truth in love at all times, including when we speak to or about one another as male or female. WE DENY any obligation to speak in such ways that dishonor God’s design of his image bearers as male and female. **Article 12** WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ gives both merciful pardon and transforming power, and that this pardon and power enable a follower of Jesus to put to death sinful desires and to walk in a manner worthy of the Lord. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ is insufficient to forgive all sexual sins and to give power for holiness to every believer who feels drawn into sexual sin. **Article 13** WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ enables sinners to forsake transgender self- conceptions and by divine forbearance to accept the God-ordained link between one’s biological sex and one’s self-conception as male or female. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ sanctions selfconceptions that are at odds with God’s revealed will. **Article 14** WE AFFIRM that Christ Jesus has come into the world to save sinners and that through Christ’s death and resurrection forgiveness of sins and eternal life are available to every person who repents of sin and trusts in Christ alone as Savior, WE DENY that the Lord’s arm is too short to save or that any sinner is beyond his reach. **Therefore be it resolved** that the Calvary Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly and asks it to declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood’s "Nashville Statement" on biblical sexuality as a biblically faithful declaration and refer the “Nashville Statement” to the Committee on Discipleship Ministries for inclusion and promotion among its denominational teaching materials. **Grounds:** “The Nashville Statement,” carefully worked out by the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood in 2017, is a timely statement that speaks into the current confusion surrounding gender and sexuality within the evangelical church (including the PCA) and the broader culture. Signed by many leaders within the Reformed and evangelical world, it is a balanced and biblically faithful attempt to “speak the truth in love” (Eph. 4:15) on one of the most pivotal and controversial issues facing the church …

source: OVERTURE 23 from Central Carolina Presbytery (to IRC)
body: “Withdraw from the National Association of Evangelicals” **Whereas** the Presbyterian Church in America is a member of the National Association of Evangelicals (NAE); and **Whereas** the label “evangelical” has come to designate political distinctives as much or more than theological commitments and distinctives; [8] and **Whereas** Chapter 31 of the _Westminster Confession of Faith_ states that “Synods and councils are to handle, or conclude nothing, but that which is ecclesiastical: and are not to intermeddle with civil affairs which concern the commonwealth, unless by way of humble petition in cases extraordinary; or, by way of advice, for satisfaction of conscience, if they be thereunto required by the civil magistrate.”; and **Whereas** PCA _BCO_ 3-3 states that “The sole functions of the Church, as a kingdom and government distinct from the civil commonwealth, are to proclaim, to administer, and to enforce the law of Christ revealed in the Scriptures.”; and **Whereas** the Scriptures clearly teach that Christians should be stewards of God’s creation, care for sojourners and aliens, and promote matters of civil justice, and members of the PCA may have legitimate differences of opinion on the most effective political policies to address these matters; and **Whereas** the NAE has stated that it intends not only to advocate for biblical values and ethics in general, but that “we must advocate for political policies;” [9] and 8 Benjamin Huskinson. “The Missing Link between Evangelicals and Trump.” The[American-Interest.com. (https://www.the-american-interest.com/2018/11/23/the-missing-](https://www.the-american-interest.com/2018/11/23/the-missing-link-between-evangelicals-and-trump/) [link-between-evangelicals-and-trump/)](https://www.the-american-interest.com/2018/11/23/the-missing-link-between-evangelicals-and-trump/) 9 National Association of Evangelicals. “For the Health of a Nation: An Evangelical Call to [Civic Responsibility.” NAE.net (https://www.nae.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/For-the-](https://www.nae.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/For-the-Health-of-the-Nation_spreads.pdf) [Health-of-the-Nation_spreads.pdf)](https://www.nae.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/For-the-Health-of-the-Nation_spreads.pdf) **Whereas** the NAE has frequently intermeddled in civil affairs, by publicly pushing for action on the environment [10], immigration [11], and has changed its original stance on the death penalty [12] ; and **Whereas** the NAE has recently passed a motion entitled “Fairness for All” [13] which, in advocating for a political compromise regarding sexual orientation, gender identity, and religious freedom, goes beyond Chapter 31 of the _Westminster Confession of Faith_ ; and **Whereas** the NAE claims to speak for all of its members and to be their voice in Washington; and **Whereas** these are only a few of many examples of the NAE’s continuing practice of intermeddling in civil affairs; and **Whereas** our sister denomination the RPCNA earlier withdrew from the NAE in 2009 citing “President Leith Anderson’s participation in the meeting between Christians and Muslims where the document ‘Loving God and Neighbor Together: A Christian Response to “A Common Word Between Us and You”’ was approved and signed,” and noting that “the document is clearly based on an unbiblical premise. It falsely assumes that Christianity and Islam approach the same God, but in different ways.” [14] ; and` **Whereas** no other NAPARC denominations are members of the NAE; the Southern Baptist Convention is not a member of the NAE; the Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod is not a member of the NAE; no Anglican bodies are members of the NAE; no predominantly African American denominations are members of the NAE; no mainline denominations are members of the NAE; the Roman Catholic Church is not a member of the NAE; and no Orthodox communions are members of the NAE; and **Whereas** the Presbyterian Church in America, as such, has no need of the benefits of membership in the NAE, especially of having a voice in Washington championing political concerns; 10 [“NAE Releases Poverty, Creation Care Document” (https://www.nae.net/nae-releases-](https://www.nae.net/nae-releases-poverty-creation-care-document/) [poverty-creation-care-document/)](https://www.nae.net/nae-releases-poverty-creation-care-document/) 11 “Evangelicals Push For Immigration Reform At Capitol Hill” - [(https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/04/29/evangelicals](https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/04/29/evangelicals-immigration-reform_n_5235516.html) immigration [reform_n_5235516.html)](https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/04/29/evangelicals-immigration-reform_n_5235516.html) 12 “The National Association of Evangelicals has changed its position on the death penalty” [(https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/acts-of-faith/wp/2015/10/19/the-national-](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/acts-of-faith/wp/2015/10/19/the-national-association-of-evangelicals-has-changed-its-position-on-the-death-penalty/) [association-of-evangelicals-has-changed-its-position-on-the-death-penalty/)](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/acts-of-faith/wp/2015/10/19/the-national-association-of-evangelicals-has-changed-its-position-on-the-death-penalty/) 13 “Boards back SOGI compromise” [(https://world.wng.org/2018/12/boards_back_sogi_compromise/) “Fairness for All](https://world.wng.org/2018/12/boards_back_sogi_compromise/) [Motion” (https://world.wng.org/sites/default/files/assets/NAEBoardResolution_0.pdf)](https://world.wng.org/sites/default/files/assets/NAEBoardResolution_0.pdf) 14 RPCNA IRC NAE Withdrawal Statement (permission granted to cite by the RPCNA Interchurch Committee) **Therefore,** Central Carolina Presbytery hereby overtures the 47 [th] General Assembly to withdraw the membership of the PCA in the NAE at the soonest possible date. _Adopted by Central Carolina Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 23, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ RE Flynt Jones, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 24 from Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (to AC, CDM,
body: “Add Constitutional Precedence Statement to MNA, MTW, RUF Policy Manuals” (Revised) CC, CTS, PCAF, PCA-RBI, RH) [Note: An earlier version of this overture appeared online in early March. At its May 4 meeting Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery revised the first “Whereas” clause to clarify the Committees and Agencies involved. There is no other change to the original overture.] **Whereas** the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) currently has five Permanent Committees (Administrative Committee, Committee on Discipleship Ministries, Mission to North America, Mission to the World, and Reformed University Fellowship) and five Agencies (Covenant College, Covenant Seminary, PCA Foundation, PCA Retirement & Benefits, Inc., and Ridge Haven), and may in the future have other or additional Permanent Committees and Agencies (all such current and future Permanent Committees and Agencies, collectively, the “Permanent Committees and Agencies”) [ _BCO_ 14.1.12; _RAO_ 14.1]; and **Whereas** it is necessary for the Permanent Committees and Agencies to function at all times under the authority of the Constitution (as defined in _BCO_ Preface III, and which includes the _Westminster Confession of_ _Faith,_ the _Larger Catechism_ and _Shorter Catechism,_ and the _Book of_ _Church Order_, collectively, the “Constitution”); [ _BCO_ 14.1.7–8; 14.6; Article V.G of the Corporate Bylaws]; and **Whereas** it is standard operating procedure for organizations to write policy manuals; and **Whereas** the Permanent Committees and Agencies rightly and necessarily have at times produced their respective policy manuals; and **Whereas** it is essential for every policy manual of the Permanent Committees and Agencies to remain subject to the Constitution; and **Whereas** it is possible for unanticipated conflicts, potential conflicts, or ambiguities to arise between Permanent Committee and Agency policy manuals and the Constitution; and **Whereas** it is a well-recognized best practice for policy manuals of organizations to explicitly state their subordination to organizational constitutional documents and by-laws; **Therefore, it is resolved** that the Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery hereby overture the 47 [th] General Assembly to add the following statement to the preface of all policy manuals of the Permanent Committees and Agencies: “At every point, this entire manual is subordinate to the entire Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America—the _Westminster_ _Standards_ and the _Book of Church Order_ . If there exists any conflict between the PCA’s constitutional documents and the content and stipulations of this manual, the Constitution carries final authority.” **Further resolved**, that any policy manual produced or amended by any of the Permanent Committees and Agencies shall, before becoming operational, be approved by its respective board and submitted to the General Assembly for ratification through the usual process of the reports of the Permanent Committees and Agencies. **Further resolved**, that each of the Permanent Committees and Agencies report back on the implementation of these actions to their respective Committee of Commissioners at the 48 [th] General Assembly. **Rationale** _**:**_ In order to carry out their responsibilities faithfully, Permanent Committees and Agencies must be able to develop and propose policies to the General Assembly for ratification. _BCO_ 14.1.7 indicates that “The Assembly's committees are to serve and not to direct any Church judicatories. They are not to establish policy, but rather execute policy established by the General Assembly.” The only effective method to ensure Permanent Committee and Agency policies yield to the PCA constitution, and the only way to ensure that constitutional due process for staff of these permanent Committees and Agencies in relation to written policies, is (1) to give the PCA constitution explicitly stated priority in all policy manuals, and (2) to make policy changes according to _BCO_ 14.1.7, which grants the General Assembly full visibility into proposed policies (and any wording changes to policies) in order to exercise its constitutionally-appointed powers of ratification. The action of the 5 [th] General Assembly, for example, delivers a clear process in relation to the Committee on Mission to the World (CMTW). This GA action (1977, p. 72, 5–64, IV, 9) differentiated between the MTW policy manual and the MTW handbook, when it determined “the policy manual to be revised only by General Assembly procedures while changes in the handbooks (which unavoidably need continual changes to meet changing situations with regard to such things as insurance, annuity, travel, etc.) be reported annually to the MTW Committee of Commissioners (CoC) at the General Assembly for their approval.” Usual process for policy changes then requires that changes/additions be submitted by CMTW to the CoC for ratification by the General Assembly, with a CMTW minute to this effect in each instance. The CoC should then include these as recommendations in their report to GA (including any minority reports). In 2014, the 42 [nd] General Assembly of the PCA passed Overture 6, “Child Protection in the PCA.” This overture directed the Permanent Agencies and Committees “to review their policies, procedures and practices in the area of child protection, including their response to child sexual abuse disclosures, their faithfulness in reporting child sexual abuse to duly appointed proper representatives of the God-ordained civil authorities, in accordance with local laws, their care for survivors of child sexual abuse, and their future plans to help educate the PCA on child sexual abuse, and all other areas of response consistent with Scripture and the Constitution of the PCA and report to the 43 [rd] General Assembly through the Administrative Committee, after it has referred the matter to and received a report from the Cooperative Ministries Committee.” We trust that …

source: OVERTURE 25 from the Suncoast Florida Presbytery (to CDM)
body: “Support Christian Education” **Whereas** the Presbyterian Church in America has seen fit to establish Covenant College and Covenant Theological Seminary to educate students in accordance with a Biblical worldview, including studies in covenantal and Reformed theology, as well as studies touching upon our Lord’s Great Commission and the extension of His Kingdom; and **Whereas** the Scriptures command faithful Biblical instruction be given to God’s covenant children as well, those little ones being brought up in the context of God’s covenant people and in accordance with their union with Christ (Deut 6:7-15; Prov. 22:6; Mt. 19:14, 15; Eph. 6:4), making a distinction between their education and that of unbelievers; and **Whereas** the wisdom of God being expressed through His people reveals itself to be “pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, and sincere…” (James 3:17); and **Whereas** a considerable number of parents in our churches, increasing in their knowledge of God’s Word and works (Ps. 78:4-7), desire an educational context for their covenant children consistent with God’s Word, a context which encourages them to rejoice in Him as Creator, Redeemer, and Lord over all; a context which encourages them to exercise dominion as His image-bearers for His honor, one which will enable them to be informed by and conformed to His Truth (John 17:17); and **Whereas** a considerable number of materialistic/secular world view ideas (such as those touching upon gender identity issues, new definitions of marriage and family, sexual boundaries, questions of who has ultimate authority over the children, etc.) become increasingly politicized and passed into law; and **Whereas** Christian families are experiencing an increase of tension in the public school arena as school policies, approved practices, classroom instruction, discussion, and textbooks oppose and in some instances, vilify, their Biblical convictions; indeed, sometimes resulting in legal action on the part of the state (more recently in reference to gender identity issues); and **Whereas** parents of baptized children make vows to bring the child up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord ( _BCO_ 56-5); and **Whereas** the congregation also makes a vow to assist these parents in the aforesaid endeavor ( _BCO_ 56-5); and **Whereas** the elders and deacons of Christ’s church work together in promoting the spiritual well-being of church members (including the covenant children) encouraging, praying, and supporting if necessary (and possible) what tends to their spiritual growth and good. ( _BCO_ 6-1, 3; _BCO_ 7-2; _BCO_ 8-3; _BCO_ 9-1; _BCO_ 12-5); **Therefore** **be it resolved** that the Presbyteries, Sessions, and Diaconates of the Presbyterian Church in America, be encouraged to embrace and provide a supportive posture for Christian education in our churches and communities by: a. Teaching on the nature, purpose, and tasks involved in bringing covenant children up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord (Ephesians 6:4). b. Faithfully addressing the challenges Christian families face who enroll their covenant children in public educational settings, seeking to provide resources and support which will equip their students to be salt and light, and to remain faithful to the truth as expressed in Christ and His Word. c. Considering/dialoguing with members in our covenant communities regarding the privileges and benefits of a wholly Christian education in which the primary goal is the development of a mind and heart consistently conformed to the worldview of the Bible as it touches upon all aspects of living in union with Christ- in God’s amazing world under Christ’s reign (Genesis 1:1; Psalm 2:6, 11, 12; Psalm 19:1; Psalm 24; Romans 12:1, 2). d. By offering, whenever possible, financial, spiritual and instructional assistance helpful to those families expressing a desire to pursue a wholly Christian education for their children. e. By encouraging the establishment of sound Christian schools in our churches and communities through prayer and support as our Lord provides. _Adopted by Suncoast Florida Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 12, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE David Stewart,_ _stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 26 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Establish Study Committee on Domestic Abuse” (Version 5) **Whereas**, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:2527; also _WLC_ 135 and 139); and **Whereas**, these sins are especially heinous because they are “against the express letter of the law,” “break many commandments,” “admit of no reparation,” and often involve various other aggravations ( _WLC_ 151); and **Whereas**, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society; and **Whereas**, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and **Whereas**, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and **Whereas,** these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and **Whereas**, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and **Whereas**, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and **Whereas**, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and **Whereas**, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; **Therefore, be it resolved** to hereby overture the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study: (1) the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault; (2) pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins; (3) pastoral resources available on the perpetrators of these sins; (4) the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them; (5) the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and (6) the possible need for repentance as a church; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and **Be it further resolved** that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly. _Adopted by Tennessee Valley Presbytery at its stated meeting, January 12, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Jacob A. Bennett_

“Study Possibility of Remote Voting at General Assembly” **Whereas**, the Presbyterian Church in America was founded as a “grass roots” denomination with power and authority flowing from the bottom up; and **Whereas**, the expense of sending a commissioner to the General Assembly has become prohibitive for many small churches in the PCA; and **Whereas**, many commissioners would attend the General Assembly, yet are unable because of health restrictions; and **Whereas**, the General Assembly meetings now have a small representation by ruling elders; and **Whereas**, it is in accordance with the founding principles of the PCA to have parity of the teaching and ruling elders in authority; and **Whereas**, it is in accordance with the founding principles of the PCA and our _BCO_ to have parity of teaching and ruling elders on General Assembly committees ( _BCO_ 14-1; Principles for the Organization of the Assembly, item 10) and to have at least parity of teaching and ruling elders at General Assembly court meetings ( _BCO_ 14-2); and **Whereas**, the technology exists to have commissioners vote on issues of the General Assembly from a distance while they watch the proceedings of the General Assembly online; and **Whereas**, the General Assembly as presently structured would continue with the exception of a distance voting commissioner; **Therefore**, Westminster Presbytery overtures the 47 [th] General Assembly to instruct the PCA Administrative Committee to investigate and report at the 48 [th] general assembly a plan to create adv c (Distance Voting Commissioner) which would entail the ability of regularly elected commissioners to vote electronically at a distance from the site of the General Assembly. _Adopted by Westminster Presbytery at its stated meeting, March 9, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Mark J. Blalack, stated clerk_

“Affirmations and Denials regarding Homosexuality **”** **Whereas** a controversy has arisen in the Presbyterian Church in America over certain teachings espoused by Revoice, an organization that is promoting LGBT+ flourishing in various PCA churches, it has become necessary to clarify and reaffirm what the Bible teaches concerning homosexuality and gender; **Therefore be it resolved** that Westminster Presbytery ask the 47 [th] General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to adopt the following 12 articles that clarify and affirm the Bible’s teaching about homosexuality and gender. **Article 1** WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction, homosexual orientation, and homosexual acts are against nature and sinful. (Rom. 1:26-27) WE DENY that homosexual attraction is part of the original creation order, since God created man in His image male and female for one another. (Gen. 1:27-28; Gen. 2:18, 21-24; Mt. 19:4-6) **Article 2** WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction is a vile, degrading, and dishonorable passion, and those who condone homosexuality invite the further judgment of God. (Rom. 1:26-32) WE DENY that unrepentant homosexuals will inherit the kingdom of God. (1 Cor. 6:9-10) **Article 3** WE AFFIRM that Jesus condemned both sinful sexual attractions and sinful sexual actions. (Mt. 5:27-28) WE DENY that scripture permits homosexual attraction and orientation. (Rom. 1:26-27) **Article 4** WE AFFIRM that those with homosexual attractions, incestuous attractions, and bestial attractions are ”sexual minorities” in the church. WE DENY that there is any virtue in being identified as a “sexual minority,” because all of these dispositions are sinful. (Lev. 18:6, 22-23; 20:13, 15-16) **Article 5** WE AFFIRM that God by His grace can change an unnatural sexual orientation. (1 Cor. 6:11; 1 Jn. 1:9) WE DENY that unnatural sexual orientations are fixed, permanent, and unchangeable. (Col. 1:21-23) **Article 6** WE AFFIRM that many people having a homosexual orientation do not desire this orientation. WE DENY that unwanted vile passions are natural, neutral, or good. (Rom. 7:21-25) **Article 7** WE AFFIRM that Christians ought to abhor homosexual sin (Lev. 18:22). Abhorrence of all sin should be cultivated. Those who love the Lord hate evil. (Ps. 97:10) WE DENY that revulsion and abhorrence of homosexual sin is sinful. (Rom. 12:9; 1 Cor. 13:4-7) **Article 8** WE AFFIRM that people living in homosexual sin should be shown kindness and lovingly encouraged to turn from their sin to serve Christ who alone can deliver them from sin and its shame. (Mk. 2:16-17; James 5:19-20) WE DENY that it is loving or kind to try to diminish or remove the shame of homosexual attraction and orientation, since God calls it shameful. (Rom. 1:26-27; Jer. 6:14-15) **Article 9** WE AFFIRM that repentant sinners turning from all unnatural attractions and trusting in Christ should be welcomed into the church as members in good standing. (1 Tim. 1:15-16) WE DENY that followers of Christ who struggle with homosexual attraction should be identified as “LGBT+ Christians,” because it dishonors Christ to identify with sinful attractions and orientations. (2 Cor. 5:16-17; 1 Cor. 6:911) **Article 10** WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction should be mortified by the power of the Spirit. (Col. 3:1-7; Rom. 8:12-14; 1 Thess. 4:3-5) WE DENY that continuing homosexual attraction or failure to attain orientation change is evidence of God’s approval of these unnatural and vile passions. (Rom. 7:21-25; Rom. 1:26-27) **Article 11** WE AFFIRM that those struggling with unlawful sexual attractions of any kind should be encouraged to seek the help, prayer, and counsel of mature believers, elders, and pastors. (James 5:16; Heb. 3:12-13; Heb. 10:24-25) WE DENY that those struggling with homosexual attraction and orientation should suffer in silence. (Gal. 6:1-2) **Article 12** WE AFFIRM that our inward self-conception and outward gender identity must conform to the sex God assigned us at conception, and thus we are to live in obedience to his call evident in our reproductive organs. (Dt. 22:5) WE DENY that physical anomalies or psychological conditions nullify the union God has decreed between biological sex and self-conception and gender identity. _Adopted by Westminster Presbytery at its stated meeting, March 9, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Mark J. Blalack, stated clerk_ **OVERTURE 29** -= **WITHDRAWN**

source: OVERTURE 30 from Illiana Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Establish Study Committee on Same-sex Orientation and Gender Identity” **Whereas,** the Fifth PCA General Assembly in 1977 affirmed “the Biblical position for our denomination which states that: (1) The act of homosexuality is a sin according to God’s Word; (2) Churches should actively seek to lead the homosexual person to confession and repentance that he might find justification and sanctification in Jesus Christ, according to 1 Corinthians 6:11; and, (3) In light of the Biblical view of its sinfulness, a practicing homosexual continuing in this sin would not be a fit candidate for ordination or membership in the Presbyterian Church in America”; and **Whereas,** the PCA General Assembly has affirmed this position on subsequent occasions, including 1996 and 1999; and **Whereas,** the Revoice Conference held at Memorial Presbyterian Church (PCA) in St. Louis, MO, has promoted questions and concerns about the PCA’s position on sexual orientation and gender identity that are not addressed in the affirmation of the Fifth General Assembly; and **Whereas,** the peace and purity of Christ’s church is under assault by the acceptance of cultural norms and misleadings concerning sexual orientation and identity; **Therefore be it resolved** that Illiana Presbytery hereby overtures the 47 [th] General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to form a study committee comprised of at least four Teaching and four Ruling Elders appointed by the Moderator, to study questions of same-sex orientation and gender identity and to develop a PCA position statement on these matters. _Adopted by Illiana Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 9, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE J. Dawson Miller_ _, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 31 from Eastern Pennsylvania Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Form an Ad Interim Committee to Address Matters Related to Domestic Abuse, Domestic Oppression, and Sexual Assault” (Version 6) **Be it resolved:** 1. That the 47th General Assembly create a seven-member Ad Interim Committee (AIC) tasked to accomplish the following. a. Prepare an annotated bibliography of recommended pastoral resources available on the nature of domestic abuse, domestic oppression, [15] and sexual assault, as well as pastoral resources for the care of victims of these sins; b. Explore these matters from an historical perspective, giving special consideration of how they have been conceived of and addressed within the Reformed tradition and provide a summary of their findings. c. Describe "best practices" and policy guidelines that could be helpful for elders, Sessions, Presbyteries, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them; d. If the Committee deems it prudent, it may include in the report any revisions or additions to _BCO_ Rules of Discipline that might more appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process, which changes may be issued as an overture to a subsequent General Assembly by any Presbytery that would wish to do so; e. If the Committee deems it prudent, it may include in the report any statement the Committee might recommend for the GA to consider adopting regarding any PCA repentance related to these matters, which statement may be issued as an overture to a subsequent General Assembly by any Presbytery that would wish to do so. 2. The 47th GA authorizes the Moderator of the 47th GA to appoint the seven voting members of this Committee. ( _RAO_ 9-4) a. These members shall be PCA ministers or PCA ruling elders, and the Committee shall include at least two of each. (Presbyteries, Sessions, and individuals may contact the Moderator with suggested names.) b. The 47th GA authorizes the Moderator to make all of his appointments after the 47th GA adjourns. ( _RAO_ 9-4) 3. The 47th GA authorizes the Moderator to appoint others to serve the Committee as advisors, regardless of gender or denominational affiliation, within the confines of its budget. The 47th GA recommends the Moderator appoint at least two women who are subject-matter experts and voting members. 15 Domestic oppression is an ongoing pattern of intimidating and domineering behavior employed by one family member to control one or more other family members. A superior/inferior, hierarchical power differential is established, maintained, and increased more and more as time goes on... domestic oppressors systematically tyrannize, intimidate, threaten, emotionally coerce, dehumanize, objectify, demean, degrade, manipulate, and bully at least one other person within the family home—usually their spouse. Source: [Rev. Warren Lamb, https://pastorlamb.com/2018/05/08/domestic-oppression-time-to-talk-](https://pastorlamb.com/2018/05/08/domestic-oppression-time-to-talk-about-i) [about-i](https://pastorlamb.com/2018/05/08/domestic-oppression-time-to-talk-about-i) 4. Budget and Funding – The AIC budget shall be $15,000, all of which shall come from contributions to the AC designated for the AIC. (The Pacific Northwest Presbytery will commit to contribute $1,000 to that end.) 5. Reporting The Committee shall either report its findings on 1.a (bibliography) and 1.c (best practices) directly to the 48th GA, or at that time request an extension ( _RAO_ 9-4). **Rationale** : 1. The sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden by Scripture and the Westminster Standards. (For example, see 2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25-27; also, _WLC_ 135 and 139.) 2. These sins are especially heinous as they are “against the express letter of the law,” “break many commandments,” “admit of no reparation,” and often involve various other aggravations ( _WLC_ 151). 3. Sadly, these sins are prevalent in our society, and in the church. [16] 4. These sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22). 5. It is the responsibility of the elders of the Church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins, with an aim toward a full repentance. 6. these sins have been a concern and a subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly. 7. In 2014, the 42nd General Assembly (Houston, TX) exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children. 16 For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: “More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime.” (Available at www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls Report titled _Sexual_ _Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements_ (Atlanta: CDC, 2014; available at [www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-](http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf) [a.pdf](http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf) ). 8. Many PCA ministers, ruling elders, and candidates report a desire to be resourced in order to provide better pastoral care on these sins and their resulting complex consequences. 9. Many PCA ministers, ruling elders, and candidates report a desire to learn of "best practices" regarding church and presbytery policies in this area. For example, some ministers and elders are unaware of the different levels of background checks that can be utilized in screening. Some do not know what their State's laws are regarding mandatory reporters or in what situations those laws may or may not apply. 10. Our _BCO_ Part II Rules of Discipline might benefit from additions or revisions that address these matters. For example, the following _BCO_ provisions might benefit from review and revision, at least in the context of a minor who accuses an adult of sexual misconduct: _BCO_ 35-1....The accused party may be allowed, but shall not be compelled to testify; but the accuser shall be required to testify, on the demand of the accused. ... _BCO_ 32-13. In order that the trial may be fair and impartial, the witnesses shall be examined in the presence of the accused, or at least after he shall have received due citation to attend. Witnesses may be cross-examined by both parties, and any questions asked must be pertinent to the issue. _BCO_ 32-20. Process, in case of scandal, shall commence within the space of one year after the offense was committed, unless it has recently become flagrant…. _BCO_ 35-4. no witness afterwards to be examined, unless a member of the court, shall be present during the examination of another witness on the same case, if either party object. 11. Reporting Recommendations through the Overtures Committee In the past, Ad Interim Committees have customarily reported recommendations directly to the GA floor. But going through the OC is a more prudent and efficient path for any AIC recommendations on _BCO_ changes and/or any recommended statement for GA adoption. Furthermore, _RAO_ 12-1 stipulates " _all_ recommendations proposing amendment to the Constitution _shall_ be referred to the Overtures Committee for their review and recommendation to the General Assembly." And this would also be the most prudent and efficient path for any _BCO_ recommendation from this AIC. The _RAO_ section on OC reports to GA provides a wiser method for handling all recommendations from the AIC: _RAO_ 15-8.c. "A recommendation [from the OC] shall be considered under the standard rules governing debate, but Subsidiary Motions ( _RRO_ VI) to _Postpone Indefinitely_, to _Amend_, to _Commit,_ and to _Limit Debate_ ; and Incidental Motions ( _RRO_ VIII) to _Divide a Question_, to _Consider_ _Seriatim_, and _Constitutional Inquiries_, shall **not** be permitted. A motion to _Recommit_ shall be permitted, but a motion to _Recommit With Instructions_ shall not be permitted." If the 2019 Dallas GA Overtures Committee, and then the Dallas GA, want recommendations from this particular AIC to go through the 2020 Birmingham OC first, that is certainly the constitutional prerogative of the commissioners in Dallas. _Adopted by Eastern Pennsylvania Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 9, 2019_ _Attested by TE Mel Farrar, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 32 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery (CCB, OC)
body: “Amend _BCO_ 14-1.10, _14-_ 1.11, and 14-1.12 to Allow Non-ordained Persons to Serve on Committees and Boards (Version 4) **Whereas**, vigorous participation of women in the life of the early church is attested by the New Testament: they helped select (Acts 1:14) and train (Acts 18:26) leaders of the church, were prophets (Acts 21:8-9), served the church through deeds of mercy in vital ways (Acts 9:36–41), were instrumental in the planting of churches (Acts 16:12–15; 17:4,12) and other missionary endeavors (Acts 18:1f), and were acknowledged as important leaders for the church (Rom. 16:3-4); and **Whereas**, the Presbyterian Church in America believes Christ has called his church to be a “spiritual commonwealth” ( _BCO_ 3-1), in which members elect godly men to be ordained as elders who are given the power of jurisdiction as they act jointly in the courts of the church ( _BCO_ 3-2); and **Whereas**, a robustly complementarian perspective affirms the oversight of these elders and the proper, vital and full expression of the gifts given by Christ to men and women for his service; and **Whereas**, as part of the calling of church leaders to “equip the saints for the work of ministry for building up the body of Christ” (Eph. 4:12), many sessions throughout the PCA identify gifted men and women to serve on committees of the church, such as missions, building, and pastoral search committees; and **Whereas**, in contrast with a commission in the PCA, which is "authorized to deliberate and conclude the business referred to it," committees are appointed by courts “to examine, consider and report” to their constituting court concerning the matters that court delegates to them ( _BCO_ 15-1) and thus do not exercise governing authority; and **Whereas**, in accordance with this principle, Permanent Committees established by the General Assembly are “to serve and not to direct any Church judicatories. They are not to establish policy, but rather execute policy established by the General Assembly” ( _BCO_ 14-1.7); and **Whereas** neither the NT evidence nor the constitutional evidence cited above seem to have been given adequate consideration by the 17th GA in their denial of O.24 asking for a study committee to determine whether "women could be included on some or all of the permanent committees and agencies of the GA," which was the precedent cited for rejecting the overtures presented last year to open participation on Boards and Permanent Committees to non-ordained members; and **Whereas**, these considerations suggest there is no impediment to an unordained member in good standing in the PCA serving on a Permanent Committee or Agency of the General Assembly established in _BCO_ 141.12; and **Whereas**, the 45th General Assembly adopted the recommendation of The Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church that stated, “sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly strive to develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom of godly women in the local, regional, and national church, and particularly consider overtures that would allow qualified women to serve on appropriate committees and agencies within the church”; and **Whereas**, the 46th General Assembly answered in the negative an overture to allow non-ordained members on General Assembly Agency Boards on the grounds that _BCO_ 14-1.11 had to be amended prior to amendment of the PCA Bylaws, which governs the Agencies, **Therefore be it resolved** to amend _The Book of Church Orde_ r 14-1.10, 14 1.11, and 14-1.12 as follows: [Proposed additions underlined and deletions noted by strike out.] _**BCO**_ **14-1.** ~~10. The committees are to be established on the basis of an~~ ~~equal number between teaching and ruling elders.~~ ~~11.1~~ 0. A Nominating Committee shall be comprised of one representative elected by each Presbytery in the following manner. Each Presbytery shall be assigned to a class by the stated clerk based on its date of formation. The members shall serve in classes of three year terms, alternating between ruling and teaching elders. When necessary, unexpired terms shall be filled by an elder of the same class, teaching or ruling. This committee is to present all nominations for which it is responsible to the next meeting of the Assembly from a slate of ~~men~~ candidates nominated by the Presbyteries. Presbyteries shall utilize the nominating forms provided by the stated clerk for their nominations. Each presbytery may present one teaching elder, ~~and~~ one ruling elder, and, when applicable, one non-elder candidate to fill openings that are designated for members at large for each committee or agency. Any non ordained person nominated must meet the qualifications outlined in _BCO_ 14-1.11. In addition to nominees for expired terms, the Committee shall nominate for each permanent Committee one ruling, ~~and~~ one teaching elder and a member at large candidate as alternates to fill any vacancies that may occur during the year. Each alternate should attend each meeting and fill any vacancy necessary to meet a quorum. In addition to the new nominees from the Presbyteries, alternates not assuming any vacancies during a year will be automatically considered by the Nominating Committee as candidates for nomination to that same committee. 11. To be qualified for nomination and election to serve on a Permanent Committee or Agency as a member at large, a non ordained candidate must be a member in good standing of a Church in the Presbyterian Church in America and must receive an endorsement from their Session. The endorsement will consist of testimony regarding the candidate’s Christian character, knowledge of and adherence to the Constitution and promise of faithful service to the General Assembly. 12. The Assembly permanent committees are the Administrative Committee of the General Assembly, Committee on Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship. The Administrative Committee of the General Assembly (AC) shall consist of twenty (20) members: a. Eleven members, six elders and five members who are not elders, shall be in classes elected through the standard nomination and election procedure, b. One member from each of the following program committees or agencies: 1. Committee on Discipleship Ministries (CDM) 2. Covenant College (CC) 3. Covenant Theological Seminary (CTS) 4. Mission to North America (MNA) 5. Mission to the World (MTW) 6. PCA Foundation (PCAF) 7. PCA Retirement & Benefits, Inc. (RBI) 8. Reformed University Fellowship (RUF) 9. Ridge Haven Conference Center (RH) The eleven elected members ~~at large~~ shall serve a term of four years. The chairman of the Administrative Committee shall be one of its elected ordained members ~~at large~~ . Each program committee and agency shall designate its member each year at the last meeting of the committee or board before the meeting of the General Assembly. The chief administrative officers of the program committees and agencies may attend any meeting of the Administrative Committee. They shall be entitled to the privilege of the floor but shall not have a vote and must be excluded when an executive session is called. Committee on Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship shall consist of fifteen (15) ~~men~~ members divided into five classes of three ~~men m~~ embers. Three classes will have one TE, one RE and one member at large. One class shall have one TE and two members at large and one class shall have one RE and two members at large. ~~each, with two men Being TEs and one~~ ~~RE or two men being REs and one TE on alternate years,~~ Each class shall be elected to serve five-year terms. Committee ~~s~~ on Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship shall have one ruling elder, ~~and~~ one teaching elder and one member at large as alternates to fill any vacancy that may occur during the year. Persons who have served for a full term, or for at least two years of a partial term, on one of the Assembly’s permanent committees or agencies shall not be eligible for re-election to an Assembly committee until one year has elapsed. (Exceptions may be permitted in agency bylaws approved by the Assembly). So that _BCO_ 14-1.10, 14-1.11, and 14-1.12 as amended would read: _**BCO**_ **14-1** 10. source: OVERTURE 33 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery (to CCB, OC)
body: “Amend _BCO_ 57-5 to Add Vow Regarding Trinity" **Whereas**, there is but one only, living, and true God, who exists as three persons—God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit—of one substance, power, and eternity (WCF 2; WLC 9; WSC 6); and **Whereas**, the doctrine of the Trinity is foundational, essential, and vital to the Christian faith; indeed, presbyteries have been instructed to give due and serious consideration to “Appendix W,” which includes the affirmation: “the confession of the Trinity is the heartbeat of the Christian religion” (as adopted by the 45 [th] General Assembly, _Minutes,_ 29 and 624); and **Whereas**, the visible church is made up of those who profess faith in the Lord Jesus Christ ( _BCO_ 2-1), and such profession of faith is a profession of the whole Christ, who is both truly God and truly man; and **Whereas**, we live ina pluralistic age, where there is confusion over the essential being of God, illustrated by the fact that the vast majority of self-professing evangelicals in America affirm that “Jesus is the first and greatest being created by God” (Ligonier Ministries and LifeWay Research, “The State of Theology” 2018); and **Whereas**, the doctrine of the Trinity has been and is currently under assault by the unbelieving world, by cults, by unitarians, and by various religions; and **Whereas**, Mormons, Jehovah’s Witnesses, and other non-Christian faiths could affirm our current membership vows as stated; and **Whereas**, the organization of a particular church in the Presbyterian Church in America includes the pronouncement and declaration of its organization in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit ( _BCO_ 5-8); and **Whereas**, when unbaptized persons apply for admission into the Church, they shall make a public profession of their faith, in the presence of the congregation, and thereupon be baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit ( _BCO_ 56-6; 57-3), as shall the children of believing parents; and **Whereas**, “every Christian Church, or union or association of particular churches, is entitled to declare the terms of admission into its communion and the qualifications of its ministers and members” (Preface to the _BCO_ II.2); and **Whereas,** at least three fellow NAPARC churches include a membership vow requiring affirmation of the Holy Trinity; and **Whereas**, the current membership vows of the Presbyterian Church in America reference “God” ( _BCO_ 57-5), but do not require faith in God as He exists in three persons; **Therefore, be it resolved** to amend the _Book of Church Order_ 57-5 by adding the following question to the membership vows [as question 2, thereby renumbering questions 2–5 as questions 3–6]: **2. Do you believe in the one, true, and living God who** **—** **exists in three persons** **God the Father, God the Son,** **and God the Holy Spirit—who are of the same** **substance, equal in power and glory?** So that the membership vows in _Book of Church Order_ 57-5 would read: **1.** **Do you acknowledge yourselves to be sinners in the** **sight of God, justly deserving His displeasure, and** **without hope save in His sovereign mercy?** **2.** **Do you believe in the one, true, and living God who** **—** **exists in three persons** **God the Father, God the** **Son, and God the Holy Spirit—who are of the same** **substance, equal in power and glory?** ~~**2.**~~ **3.** **Do you believe in the Lord Jesus Christ as the Son** **of God, and Savior of sinners, and do you receive** **and rest upon Him alone for salvation as He is** **offered in the Gospel?** ~~**3.**~~ **4.** **Do you now resolve and promise, in humble** **reliance upon the grace of the Holy Spirit, that you** **will endeavor to live as becomes the followers of** **Christ?** ~~**4.**~~ **5.** **Do you promise to support the Church in its** **worship and work to the best of your ability?** ~~**5.**~~ **6.** **Do you submit yourselves to the government and** **discipline of the Church, and promise to study its** **purity and peace?** _Adopted by the Tennessee Valley Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 13, 2019_ _Attested by TE Jacob A. Bennett, stated clerk_
