body: “Amend _BCO_ 42-4; 43-2; and 43-3 as well as CCB, OC; _OMSJC_ 18.10 b. to Clarify Filing Requirements _OMSJC_ amendment and Allow Electronic Filings” to SJC) **Whereas,** the _Operating Manual of the Standing Judicial Commission_ ( _OMSJC_ ) explicitly prohibits filings by electronic means, as set forth in _OMSJC_ 18.10.b: Documents required or permitted to be filed by a party shall be filed with the Stated Clerk. Such filing shall not be timely unless the documents are received in the office of the Stated Clerk within the time fixed for such filing, except that papers shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if sent by certified, registered, priority, or express mail of the United States Postal Service or any delivery service where verifying receipt is utilized. **Neither facsimiles nor E-mail will be allowed for** **purposes of filing.** Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non-delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party.” (emphasis added) and **Whereas,** it is unspecified in _BCO_ 42-4, _BCO_ 43-2, and _BCO_ 43-3 whether facsimiles or email may be allowed for the purposes of filing written notice of an appeal or complaint; and **Whereas,** the provisions in _The_ _Book of Church Order_ related to filings were created before the advent of any generally available and reliable electronic communications; **Whereas,** filings by electronic means are permitted, and in some instances, mandated, in civil and criminal courts in the United States; **Whereas,** Church courts and individuals may be uncertain or confused about whether electronic filings are valid; **Whereas,** Appendix H of the _BCO_ suggests that a Presbytery Commission could accept electronic filings: At its discretion and with the consent of both parties, the Commission may decide to accept email, fax or similar means for filings after establishing procedures to confirm the date that a document is filed and received. **Whereas,** procedural errors in filing often result from the current requirement of simultaneous filings with the lower and higher court, and courts have greater expertise in such matters than individuals; **Whereas,** it is in the interest of procedural justice to preserve a uniform process of filing between lower courts and higher courts of the Presbyterian Church in America so that its members might not have their constitutional rights of appeal or complaint denied them by obscurity and unclarity in the _BCO_, and incongruence of procedures between lower and higher courts; **Therefore,** the Philadelphia Presbytery overtures to amend _BCO_ 42-4, _BCO_ 43-2, and _BCO_ 43-3 and _OMSJC_ 18.10.b as follows: [Proposed additions underlined and deletions noted by strike out.] **42-4.** Notice of appeal may be given the court before its adjournment. Written notice of appeal, ~~with~~ including supporting reasons (an “Appeal Notice”), shall be filed by the appellant with ~~both the clerk of the lower court and~~ the clerk of the higher court, within thirty (30) days of notification of the last court’s decision. With respect to the notice of appeal and the notification of the last court’s decision, the following provisions shall apply: a. An Appeal Notice shall not be timely unless received by the clerk within the time fixed for such Appeal Notice, except that an Appeal Notice shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if sent by certified, registered, priority, or express mail of the United States Postal Service or any delivery service where verifying receipt is utilized. Filing an Appeal Notice by facsimile or e-mail will be allowed and shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of confirmed receipt. Clerks of courts shall (1) make reasonable efforts to publicize addresses (both physical and electronic) to which Appeal Notices may be sent and (2) acknowledge as soon as practical the receipt of a facsimile or e-mail filing of an Appeal Notice. Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party and that the filing party bears the burden of proving that a facsimile or e-mail filing was timely made. b. Notification of the last court’s decision shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of mailing (if certified, registered or express mail of a national postal service or any private service where verifying receipt is utilized), the day of hand delivery, or the day of confirmed receipt in the case of email or facsimile. Furthermore, compliance with such requirements shall be deemed to have been fulfilled if a party cannot be located after diligent inquiry or if a party refuses to accept delivery. No attempt should be made to circularize the courts to which appeal is being made by either party before the case is heard. c. Within ten (10) days of receiving the Appeal Notice, the higher court shall send a copy of the Appeal Notice to the lower court, together with a request for the Record of the Case (as set forth in _BCO_ 42-5). **43-2.** A complaint shall first be made to the court whose act or decision is alleged to be in error. Written notice of complaint, ~~with~~ including supporting reasons (a “Complaint Notice”), shall be filed with the clerk of the court within sixty (60) days following the meeting of the court. A Complaint Notice shall not be timely unless received by the clerk within the time fixed for the Complaint Notice, except that a Complaint Notice shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if sent by certified, registered, priority, or express mail of the United States Postal Service or any delivery service where verifying receipt is utilized. Filing a Complaint Notice by facsimile or e-mail will be allowed and shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of confirmed receipt. Clerks of courts shall (1) make reasonable efforts to publicize addresses (both physical and electronic) to which Complaint Notices may be sent and (2) acknowledge as soon as practical the receipt of a facsimile or email filing of a Complaint Notice. Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party and that the filing party bears the burden of proving that a facsimile or e-mail filing was timely made. The court shall consider the complaint at its next stated meeting, or at a called meeting prior to its next stated meeting. No attempt should be made to circularize the court to which complaint is being made by either party. **43-3.** If, after considering a complaint, the court alleged to be delinquent or in error is of the opinion that it has not erred, and denies the complaint, the complainant may take that complaint to the next higher court. If the lower court fails to consider the complaint against it by or at its next stated meeting, the complainant may take that complaint to the next higher court. ~~Written~~ A Complaint Notice ~~notice thereof~~ shall be filed with ~~both the clerk of the lower court and~~ the clerk of the higher court within thirty (30) days of notification of the last court’s decision. With respect to the complaint to the next higher court and the notification of the last court’s decision, the following provisions shall apply: a. a complaint notice to a higher courts hall include a copy of the complaint that was filed with the lower court. A Complaint Notice shall not be timely unless received by the clerk within the time fixed for the Complaint Notice, except that the Complaint Notice shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if sent by certified, registered, priority, or express mail of the United States Postal Service or any delivery service where verifying receipt is utilized. Filing a Complaint Notice by facsimile or e-mail will be allowed and shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of confirmed receipt. Clerks of courts shall (1) make reasonable efforts to publicize addresses (both physical and electronic) to which Complaint Notices may be sent and (2) acknowledge as soon as practical the receipt of a facsimile or e-mail filing of a Complaint Notice. Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party and that the filing party bears the burden of proving that a facsimile or email filing was timely made. b. Notification of the last court’s decision shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of mailing (if certified, registered or express mail of a national postal service or any private service where verifying receipt is utilized), the day of hand delivery, or the day of confirmed receipt in the case of e-mail or facsimile. Furthermore, compliance with such requirements shall be deemed to have been fulfilled if a party cannot be located after diligent inquiry or if a party refuses to accept delivery. No attempt should be made to circularize the courts to which appeal is being made by either party before the case is heard. c. Within ten (10) days of receiving the Complaint Notice, the higher court shall send a copy of the Complaint Notice to the lower court, together with a request for the response of the lower court, if any, and any papers bearing on the complaint (as set forth in _BCO_ 43-6). **OMSJC 18.10** b. Documents required or permitted to be filed by a party shall be filed with the Stated Clerk. Such filing shall not be timely unless the documents are received in the office of the Stated Clerk within the time fixed for such filing, except that papers shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if sent by certified, registered, priority, or express mail of the United States Postal Service or any delivery service where verifying receipt is utilized. Filing by facsimile or e-mail will be allowed and shall be deemed to have occurred on the day of confirmed receipt. ~~Neither facsimiles nor E-mail will be allowed~~ ~~for purposes of filing.~~ Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non-delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party and that the filing party bears the burden of proving that a facsimile ore mail filing was timely made.” _Adopted by Philadelphia Presbytery at its stated meeting, March 16, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Greg Hobaugh, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 35 from Savannah River Presbytery (to OC)
body: “Affirm the PCA’s Commitment to the Sanctity of Biblical Sexual Relationships” **Whereas,** the Scripture is infallible and inerrant, the only rule of faith and practice, and the only touchstone of truth; and **Whereas**, the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America “is subject to and subordinate to the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments;” and **Whereas,** every officer (teaching elders, ruling elders, and deacons) in the Presbyterian Church in America vows that they “believe the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, as originally given, to be the inerrant Word of God, the only infallible rule of faith and practice;” and **Whereas**, all church courts in the Presbyterian Church in America have the power “to bear testimony against error in doctrine and immorality,” “to require obedience to the laws of Christ,” and “to cut off the contumacious and impenitent from the congregation of believers” ( _BCO_ 11-2); and **Whereas**, every PCA Presbytery has power “to condemn erroneous opinions which injure the purity and peace of the Church” ( _BCO_ 13-9f); and **Whereas**, the Revoice Conference, held at Memorial Presbyterian Church in St. Louis, Missouri on July 26-28, 2018, was for the purpose of “Supporting, encouraging, and empowering gay, lesbian, same-sex attracted and other LGBT+ Christians;” and **Whereas**, some within the Presbyterian Church in America are claiming that same-sex attraction is not necessarily a sin but can be a disposition given to some: “that such a disposition of sinful desires are God given for the acceptance of all believers and the Church, and for the promotion of the Glory of God;” or “that individuals with sinful homosexual feelings of same-sex attraction have no control over these feelings and/or attractions; that though they may be unwanted, they are helpless to avoid and are in no need of repentance;” or who answer affirmatively: “Can a person claim to be born with same-sex attraction in the same manner as the man born blind?” or are in agreement with: “I believe my same-sex attractions are broken, but I do not believe they are sinful. It is not sinful for me to be attracted to another man;” or asserting that same-sex attraction and orientation are permissible under the Gospel as long as the person remains celibate; even though these assertions are contrary to what Jesus said that any and all lust in the heart is a sin: “I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart” (Matthew 5:28); and **Whereas,** the Scripture teaches that same-sex attraction is an evidence that God has given over such people to “the lusts of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them” and “to degrading passions” in which “women exchanged the natural function for that which is unnatural” and “the men abandoned the natural function of the woman and burned in their desire toward one another” because they “exchanged the truth of God for a lie” and “did not see fit to acknowledge God any longer” (Romans 1:24-28); and **Whereas,** homosexuality is a sin from which God delivered some of the Corinthian Christians (“such **were** some of you…): “Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived; neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor homosexuals, nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God. Such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God” (1 Corinthians 6:9-11); and continues to deliver believers from this and other sins; and **Whereas,** same-sex attraction is lust in the very same manner that heterosexual attraction is lust, and both are violations of the seventh commandment as the Larger Catechism teaches: Question 138: What are the duties required in the seventh commandment? Answer: The duties required in the seventh commandment are, chastity in body, mind, affections, words, and behavior; and the preservation of it in ourselves and others; watchfulness over the eyes and all the senses; temperance, keeping of chaste company, modesty in apparel; marriage by those that have not the gift of continency, conjugal love, and cohabitation; diligent labor in our callings; shunning all occasions of uncleanness, and resisting temptations thereunto. Question 139: What are the sins forbidden in the seventh commandment? Answer: The sins forbidden in the seventh commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required, are, adultery, fornication, rape, incest, sodomy, and all unnatural lusts; all unclean imaginations, thoughts, purposes, and affections; all corrupt or filthy communications, or listening thereunto; wanton looks, impudent or light behavior, immodest apparel; prohibiting of lawful, and dispensing with unlawful marriages; allowing, tolerating, keeping of stews, and resorting to them; entangling vows of single life, undue delay of marriage; having more wives or husbands than one at the same time; unjust divorce, or desertion; idleness, gluttony, drunkenness, unchaste company; lascivious songs, books, pictures, dancings, stage plays; and all other provocations to, or acts of uncleanness, either in ourselves or others. **Therefore**, be it resolved, that in light of the fact that this current issue is once again confronting the PCA, the 47 [th] General Assembly take the following actions: **That** the 47 [th] General Assembly reaffirm the action of the 5 [th] General Assembly: Whereas God's Word teaches in the Old Testament that homosexuality is a sin, labeling it an “abomination" in such passages as Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13, and clearly viewing it as sin in the story of Sodom in Genesis 19:1-11; and Whereas the New Testament reaffirms the sinfulness of this “unnatural'' practice in such passages as Romans 1:26, 27 and Jude 7, even stating in 1 Corinthians 6:9-11 that homosexuals will not inherit the kingdom of heaven; Therefore, be it resolved that the Fifth General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America affirm the Biblical position for our denomination which states that: 1. The act of homosexuality is a sin according to God’s Word; 2. Churches should actively seek to lead the homosexual person to confession and repentance that he might find justification and sanctification in Jesus Christ, according to I Corinthians 6:11; and 3. In light of the Biblical view of its sinfulness, a practicing homosexual continuing in this sin would not be a fit candidate for ordination or membership in the Presbyterian Church in America. [(http://pcahistory.org/ga/5th_pcaga_1977.pdf p. 68).](http://pcahistory.org/ga/5th_pcaga_1977.pdf%20p.%2068) **Further**, that the 47 [th] General Assembly reaffirm the declaration of the 21 [st] PCA General Assembly: Therefore, the 21 [st] General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America makes the following declaration: The Bible, which is our infallible rule of faith and practice, commands us to express redemptive love and compassion to all persons. It further commands us to condemn sexual behavior which deviates from God's revealed standard as sinful and destructive. The Bible calls all who engage in these behaviors to repentance by turning to God and proving their repentance by their deeds. The chaplains of the Presbyterian Church in America are committed to providing a compassionate, redemptive, and caring ministry to military service members, their families, and other groups among whom they are called to minister regardless of sexual behavior or the diseases with which their constituents may be afflicted. Therefore, Presbyterian Church in America chaplains endorsed by the Presbyterian and Reformed Joint Commission on Chaplains and Military Personnel will continue to preach and minister in light of the whole counsel of God on these matters. [(http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf](http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf) pp. 94-95) **And further**, that the 47 [th] General Assembly reaffirm the principles regarding the biblical teachings on homosexuality contained in the "A Declaration of Conscience Addressed to the President of the United States of America" adopted by the 21st PCA General [Assembly (http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf, pp. 129-](http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf) 132). The letter said in part: Mr. President, in this Declaration the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America humbly declares its conscience concerning the moral legitimacy of homosexuality. God has spoken without equivocation through His Word declaring homosexuality to be a perversion of His created order, His moral law, and the foundations of society…. In particular, we feel compelled of conscience to speak because of the slanderous way in which truth has been portrayed, as if opposition to homosexual practice is merely a matter of prejudice against a minority. Please be informed that to act on this basis is to misjudge the issue entirely. This is a question of moral principle, striking at the very root of God's authority, man's created nature, and the structure and preservation of human society. We do not act out of a hateful prejudice which rejects the rights of minority peoples and seeks to exclude them from our communities. On the contrary, we affirm and rejoice in the God-created differences among the peoples of the world and we condemn prejudice as contrary to the heart of the gospel by which we live: that Jesus Christ is by His grace making of various peoples one community of love and fellowship. As His disciples we are called to judge, not by appearances, but to judge righteous judgment (John 7:24). The God we serve has made it plain that with Him there is no partiality, and that in this we must be like Him (Romans 2:11, James 2:1-9). As citizens we support the recognition and protection of the civil rights of all peoples. And yet in perfect consistency with this commitment we stand resolutely opposed to homosexual practice as incompatible with the temporal good of our nation and the eternal good of its people. As a part of the Church of Jesus Christ, the Presbyterian Church in America has a primary concern for the spiritual well-being of women and men created in the image of God. Responsibility to such a calling will thrust us into irreconcilable conflict with any government policy ostensibly approving a way of life under its sphere of responsibility which is contrary to the eternal good of its citizens. Further, such approval would be a grievous violation of the government's own Godordained calling (Romans 13:1-4)…. together a man and a woman, united outwardly in the institution of marriage, united inwardly in love and affection, and united physically in sexual relations, are the means of transmitting and nurturing life, and that life, growing and flourishing in families, is the necessary foundation of all society. homosexuality is a violation of these creation ordinances: it is a perversion of human nature, the gift of sexuality and the social order…. Here nature itself, the land personified, is portrayed as revolted by homosexuality as a perversion of God's purposes. Lest this be thought of as an outmoded and unenlightened perspective, the New Testament affirms this same truth with even greater clarity when it excludes, not merely from the land of Israel, but from the eternal Kingdom of God, those who pursue homosexual practice…. Please note: in condemning homosexual practice we claim no self-righteousness. The Bible we cite also teaches that all particular sins flow from one rebellious disposition of heart, a disposition of heart that belongs to all (Ephesians 2:1- 3). If we have been preserved from this perversion, it is only by God's mercy. And that mercy in Jesus Christ is so broad and free that may extend even to those caught up in …

source: OVERTURE 36 from Savannah River Presbytery (to CCB, OC)
body: “Amend _BCO_ 40-4 and 40-5 To Clarify the Meaning of ‘Credible Report’” **Whereas,** there has been various interpretations regarding the meaning of “credible report” in _BCO_ 40-5; and **Whereas**, these various interpretations have contended either that (1) a credible report may arise from any credible source presented to the court having appellate jurisdiction with respect to the court next below; or (2) a credible report may arise only upon referral of a matter from the General Assembly according to _RAO_ 16-10.c; and **Whereas**, _BCO_ 40-4 allows that: “Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be distinctly recorded by them.” and **Whereas**, _BCO_ 40-4 also states that: “If, therefore, the next higher court be well advised that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part of the lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the same, and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter as completely as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up by review of its records.” and **Whereas**, consequently when a court next below neglects to perform its duty under the Constitution; and further, fails to record its actions distinctly, the remedy is for the court with appellate jurisdiction to “be well advised that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred;” and **Whereas**, since it is not clearly defined by what means the appellate court may “be well advised that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred;” and **Whereas**, when the lower court fails to distinctly record its actions as required, and further does not inform members who may be affected and harmed by these actions with notice in a timely manner, it results in members losing their right to file an Appeal ( _BCO_ 42) or a Complaint ( _BCO_ 43) in a timely manner; and **Whereas**, courts can fail in the proper exercise of their responsibility to distinctly record their actions in such a manner that it is not discerned or discovered by the higher court during the process of the regular review of the lower court’s records, the higher court during its review of records is not able to determine or judge the validity of the record; and **Whereas**, _BCO_ 40-4 and _BCO_ 40-5 grant the higher court the right to review the record again once the higher court has received credible reports of “any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of such court;” and these credible reports can come from any credible source, which then requires the higher court to review “any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of such court.” **Therefore**, to clarify the meaning of “credible reports” this overture recommends that _BCO_ 40-4 and _BCO_ 40-5 be amended with the following (additional wording underlined): 40-4. Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be distinctly recorded by them. In any of these cases their records will by no means exhibit to the higher court a full view of their proceedings. If, therefore, the next higher court be well advised, through a credible report as defined in _BCO_ 40-5, that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part of the lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the same, and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter as completely as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up by review of its records. 40-5. When any court having appellate jurisdiction shall receive a credible report, with respect to the court next below of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of such court, the first step shall be to cite the court alleged to have offended to appear before the court having appellate jurisdiction, or its commission, by representative or in writing, at a specified time and place, and to show what the lower court has done or failed to do in the case in question. A credible report may arise either from a review of the records of the lower court as required under _BCO_ 40-1; or from other credible means that make known to the court having appellate jurisdiction of the court next below of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; and/or where the right of members to file a timely Appeal ( _BCO_ 42) or Complaint ( _BCO_ 43) was abridged by a lower court’s failure to conduct proper proceedings or to provide timely notices. When a court acts on any credible report, the parties shall be the lower court and the court having appellate jurisdiction. The court thus issuing the citation may reverse or redress the proceedings of the court below in other than judicial cases; or it may censure the delinquent court; or it may remit the whole matter to the delinquent court with an injunction to take it up and dispose of it in a constitutional manner; or it may stay all further proceedings in the case; as circumstances may require. As amended the provision would read: 40-4. Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be distinctly recorded by them. In any of these cases their records will by no means exhibit to the higher court a full view of their proceedings. If, therefore, the next higher court be well advised, through a credible report as defined in _BCO_ 40-5, that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part of the lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the same, and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter as completely as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up by review of its records. 40-5. When any court having appellate jurisdiction shall receive a credible report, with respect to the court next below of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of such court, the first step shall be to cite the court alleged to have offended to appear before the court having appellate jurisdiction, or its commission, by representative or in writing, at a specified time and place, and to show what the lower court has done or failed to do in the case in question. A credible report may arise either from a review of the records of the lower court as required under _BCO_ 40-1; or from other credible means that make known to the court having appellate jurisdiction of the court next below of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; and/or where the right of members to file a timely Appeal ( _BCO_ 42) or Complaint ( _BCO_ 43) was abridged by a lower court’s failure to conduct proper proceedings or to provide timely notices. In these cases, the parties shall be the lower court and the court having appellate jurisdiction. The court thus issuing the citation may reverse or redress the proceedings of the court below in other than judicial cases; or it may censure the delinquent court; or it may remit the whole matter to the delinquent court with an injunction to take it up and dispose of it in a constitutional manner; or it may stay all further proceedings in the case; as circumstances may require. _Adopted by Savannah River Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 16, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ RE William Hatcher, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 37 from James River Presbytery (to OC)
body: “Assembly Statement on Same-sex Attraction” **Whereas**, there is tremendous cultural pressure in the United States in these days concerning homosexuality and sexual sin; and **Whereas**, there are many people inside and outside the church who struggle with same-sex attraction and gender confusion; and **Whereas**, the Revoice organization held a conference in 2018 which discussed how to improve the way the church ministers to people who struggle with same-sex attraction, encouraging them to uphold the Biblical sexual ethic; and **Whereas**, we acknowledge and affirm that Revoice showed love to people struggling with these sins; and **Whereas**, we acknowledge and affirm that the Church has not always shown love to people who struggle with these sins; and **Whereas**, the Presbyterian Church in America, as part of its duty under the Great Commission, desires to better minister to people who struggle with same-sex attraction; **Whereas**, the Church commends the faithfulness of Christians struggling with same-sex attraction who are seeking to remain faithful to a Biblical sexual ethic; **Therefore**, the 47th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America affirms that: 1. That all persons are born sinners justly deserving God’s wrath and condemnation and inherit both the guilt of our first parents as well as corruption. (Rom 5:12) 2. That outside of Christ, men and women are enslaved to corruption which enslaves the thinking of all persons and distorts God’s created order. (Eph 2:1-8) 3. That Christ has purchased not only the faith of his saints on the cross by which they are made just in God’s sight but has also broken the power of sin/corruption to enslave His sheep. (Rom 8:1-11) 4. That Christ unites sinners to Himself, though they be corrupt through and through, but he does not leave them in corruption but subdues their corruption and produces holiness in them. (Rom 5:12-22, 6:110; Col. 2:15) 5. That corruption draws all toward sinful desires whether they be anger, disobedience, pride, hatred, lusts, or unnatural attractions. (Eph 2:1-3). 6. That the Scriptures consistently exhort believers to reckon themselves dead to sin/corruption and alive to Christ (Rom 6:5-11, 1 Cor 6:9-11) 7. That “sexual orientation” is a modern invention describing men and women as being on a spectrum of sexual attraction or desire, and is not a Biblical category. 8. That the use of terms such as “Gay Christian,” “Same Sex Attracted Christian,” “Alcoholic Christian,” “Lustful Christian,” “Greedy Christian,” or any other corrupt desire is not consistent with our union with Christ. Such descriptors of our fallenness must not be used as an identity marker but must rather be humbly submitted to Christ who provides our primary identity as Christians. (1 Cor. 6:9-11) 9. That the pull toward same-sex lust is not morally neutral but arises from our fallen nature, and with all other temptations must be mortified by the power which Christ supplies. (Rom. 1:18-27) 10. That Christians will struggle all their lives with sin and that the Church should never promise healing from sin in this life but the Spirit’s strength to kill unholy desires and to grow holy desires. (Rom 8:9-11) 11. That no temptation has overtaken any of us except that which is common to man and the Church must, therefore, be a place where we encourage one another in the battle against indwelling sin. (1 Cor 10:13) 12. That while there is a place for conferences and support groups, the Church is a haven for sinners and we should find solidarity in this common battle with sin not only with others who struggle exactly the same but primarily among those in our local congregation who share a common Savior. (Hebrews 10:25, Gal. 6:10) _Adopted by James River Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 13, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ RE Jeremy L. Pryor, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 38 from Georgia Foothills Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Establish a Study Committee on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault” (Version 7) **Whereas**, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:2527; also _WLC_ 135 and 139); and **Whereas**, these sins are especially heinous because they are “against the express letter of the law,” “break many commandments,” “admit of no reparation,” and often involve various other aggravations ( _WLC_ 151); and **Whereas**, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society; [17] and **Whereas**, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and **Whereas**, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their 17 For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: “More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime” (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled _Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data_ _Elements_ (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online at [http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_ surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf).](http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_%20surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf) care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and **Whereas,** these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and **Whereas**, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and **Whereas**, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and **Whereas**, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and **Whereas**, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; **Therefore, be it resolved** that the Georgia Foothills Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study: (1) the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault; (2) the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins; (3) the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them; (4) the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and (5) the possible need for repentance as a church; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and **Be it further resolved** that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with the Georgia Foothills Presbytery committed to offer $1,000; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly. _Adopted by Georgia Foothills Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 9, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Don Aldin, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 39 from Southern New England Presbytery (to OC)
body: “Re-commend the Previous Statements and Study Reports of the PCA in Regard to Homosexuality” **Whereas**, the Fifth General Assembly of the PCA in 1977 affirmed “the Biblical position for our denomination which states that: (1) The act of homosexuality is a sin according to God’s Word; (2) Churches should actively seek to lead the homosexual person to confession and repentance that he might find justification and sanctification in Jesus Christ, according to 1 Corinthians 6:11; and, (3) In light of the Biblical view of its sinfulness, a practicing homosexual continuing in this sin would not be a fit candidate for ordination or membership in the Presbyterian Church in America.” **(** _Minutes of the 5th_ _General Assembly_ _of the PCA_, 1977, pp. 67-68); and **Whereas**, the PCA General Assembly has reaffirmed its position on the issue of homosexuality on subsequent occasions, including 1996, 1999, and 2018; and **Whereas**, the 158th General Synod of the RPCES adopted a study report on homosexuality and commended their report, entitled “Pastoral Care for the Repentant Homosexual,” to their sessions and congregations as an aid for their ministry to those struggling with homosexuality” (158th General Synod _Minutes_, 4 July 1980, pp. 43-50; _Documents of Synod_, pp. 301-8 http://www.pcahistory.org/findingaids/rpces/docsynod/301.html); and **Whereas**, the 9th General Assembly of the PCA in 1981 adopted the Ad Interim Committee report on Joining and Receiving, which included the statement: “In receiving these denominations, the Presbyterian Church in America recognizes the history of the respective denominations as part of her total history and receives their historical documents as valuable and significant material which will be used in the perfecting of the church” [ _Minutes of the 9th_ _General Assembly of the PCA_, p. 305]. **Therefore, be it resolved**, that the Southern New England Presbytery overture the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to re-commend the previous statements and study reports of the PCA, including our study report adopted by the 158th General Synod of the RPCES on homosexuality entitled “Pastoral Care for the Repentant Homosexual,” with the deletion of Sections III and IV, to our sessions and congregations as an aid for their ministry to those struggling with homosexuality.” [158th General Synod _Minutes_, 4 July 1980, pp. 43-50; _Documents of Synod_, pp. 301-308. [http://www.pcahistory.org/](http://www.pcahistory.org/%20findingaids/%20rpces/docsynod/301.html%5d.) [findingaids/ rpces/docsynod/301.html].](http://www.pcahistory.org/%20findingaids/%20rpces/docsynod/301.html%5d.) _Adopted by Southern New England Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 27, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Ron Heald, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 40 from Northwest Georgia Presbytery (to OC)
body: “Overture for Sessions to Acknowledge and Support Women Leaders without Delay or More Divisiveness” **Whereas**, the PCA has devoted many hours of debate, study, and discussion to the role of women in the church—and such does not seem to be yielding progress or resolution but rather much distraction from mission, along with much quarreling and divisiveness (1 Cor. 6:7); and **Whereas**, a recent _Ad Interim_ Committee recommended commissioning women to serve other women and their ministry in the local church; and **Whereas**, each local church may and should use the gifts of women as that local church sees fit, under the authority and norms of Scripture—and the Resolution below requires no higher court voting or constitutional amendment; and **Whereas**, the PCA has an institution already in existence that could launch and nurture many gifts for ministry by our godly sisters, with no required _BCO_ changes or time-consuming debates; and **Whereas**, most of our female members do not desire ordination as an aspiration or prerequisite to carry out gospel ministry; and **Whereas**, rather than dividing and quarreling over this matter in the years to come; and **Whereas**, _BCO_ 9-7 presently allows Sessions to recruit godly women in ministries in the local church under the authority and norms of Scripture; and **Whereas**, Paul differentiates between the Deacons and The Women in 1 Timothy 3:8-12; and **Whereas**, the PCA could devote itself more to mission, evangelism, unity, and edification by implementing the Resolution below, rather than dividing over this issue in the courts of the church; **Therefore, be it resolved** that those churches wishing to acknowledge and support Women leaders be authorized to select and appoint the officers of their Women in the Church [previously known as WIC, or more recently “Women’s Ministry”] with the laying on of hands to serve in the local church and assist the deacons in caring for those in need and distress. The manner of appointment or election of these officers shall be the discretion of each Session. _Adopted by Northwest Georgia Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 2, 2019_ _Attested by TE Paul Legree Finch Jr., stated clerk_

“Direct CMTW to Amend its Guidelines to Implement CMTW’s ‘Statement on Valuing Women in MTW,’ so that only Ordained Elders Will Be Allowed to Serve in the Roles of Team Leader, Regional Director, and International Director within MTW.” **Whereas** on January 9, 2019, the Committee on Mission To the World (CMTW) adopted a “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW”; and **Whereas** MTW subsequently proposed guidelines to implement the “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW” that were distributed to missionaries on January 11, 2019; and **Whereas** the MTW guidelines affirm “that women may serve in leadership roles within MTW, recognizing that only ordained elders exercise ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches” [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 3, paragraph 3.]; and **Whereas** the MTW guidelines also affirm “there has been no MTW policy regarding women serving in these leadership roles…” [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 4, paragraph 1.]; and **Whereas** the MTW guidelines initiate a new policy that allows women to serve in authority over men within MTW in the roles of team leader, regional director, and international director [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 8, #3.]; and **Whereas** Heritage Presbytery and other presbyteries of the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) are charged to provide spiritual oversight for ordained elders who come from within our bounds, but who serve under MTW [See _BCO_ 8-3 &13-2.]; **Therefore be it resolved** that Heritage Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to direct CMTW to ensure that MTW amend its guidelines to implement CMTW’s “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW,” so that only ordained elders will be allowed to serve in the roles of team leader, regional director, and international director within MTW. **Rationale:** While CMTW’s intention of “supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW’s global ministry…” [see the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 698] is commendable, the MTW guidelines actually hinder some of our women from serving in MTW by creating an untenable crisis of conscience for them. Therefore, the MTW guidelines discourage some of the very sisters in Christ that CMTW’s “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW” intends to support in their missionary service. Secondly, them tw guidelines allow a woman to hold a position of authority within MTW in which she cannot exercise ecclesiastical authority over a man. And the MTW guidelines concede this would require an ordained man to fulfill some of her position’s responsibilities. [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 700, #3.] But an obvious consequence of such an awkward arrangement would be questions about what a woman in such a position is and is not allowed to do. For example, MTW’s Policy Manual currently indicates the team leader position has very broad authority, including “spiritual care” over those on the missionary team. Yet the MTW guidelines leave the team leader position potentially open to non-elders. Therefore, the MTW guidelines are unwise because they can lead to placing women in difficult positions, while causing unnecessary confusion and conflict within a missionary team. Lastly, the MTW guidelines cite the Report of the Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church to the 45th General Assembly of the PCA, as a primary reason MTW is allowing women to have authority over men within MTW – even potentially over ordained elders. [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 698.] But the 46th General Assembly rejected two overtures that would have allowed women to serve on PCA agency boards. [See Overtures 13 and 26.] _Adopted by Heritage Presbytery at its stated meeting, May 14, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ RE Conrad W Judy Jr., Stated Clerk_ **Attachment** **Statement on Valuing Women in MTW** Adopted by the Committee on Mission to the World January 9, 2019 Statement Adopted by Committee on Mission to the World: MTW values all women as created in the image of God. Under Scripture's authority and in our doctrinal view of ordination, we affirm that female disciples of Christ are co-heirs of the kingdom, co-laborers in the work of the gospel, gifted by the Spirit as members of the body of Christ and called to use these gifts for the building up of the Church and for the extension of the Kingdom of God throughout the world. Furthermore, the MTW community deeply needs the gifts and glory of God uniquely expressed in women. Therefore, MTW is committed to supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW's global ministry as together we show and tell the gospel of God's grace. In keeping with this statement, we affirm that women may serve in leadership roles within MTW, recognizing that only ordained elders exercise ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches. **Reasons for Creation of the Statement:** First, the growing desire from our denomination to encourage women to use their gifts for the service of the church are reflected in the recommendation passed at the 45 [th] General Assembly of the PCA, stating “that sessions, presbyteries, and the General Assembly strive to develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge and wisdom of godly women in the local, regional, and national church …” The spirit of this recommendation is to actively look for ways in which women can utilize their gifts in the local and larger church context. Second, women have been serving in various leadership capacities in MTW on different fields, in the home office, and in specific roles. In each of these contexts, those who made these appointments ensured that their leadership is in accord with our complementarian view of men and women’s roles in the church. The problem that emerged, however, was when women leaders were invited to global leadership meetings, questions arose from other MTW leaders and missionaries as to whether women should attend those meetings, and about the legitimacy of female leadership roles in light of passages such as 1 Timothy 2:12. What has complicated the matter is the fact that there has been no MTW policy regarding women serving in these leadership roles, nor has there been an organization-wide discussion on these issues. What has resulted is that faithful women serving in leadership are put in difficult positions, having to defend their leadership positions and presence at leadership meetings. It is in this context that we have initiated a discussion on women serving in leadership in MTW, and on deploying the God-given gifting of our MTW women, for the service of the Church. Field leadership has participated in this discussion in various ways, including writing of papers expressing a variety of opinion submitted to Committee on Mission to the World (CMTW). These discussions and papers were used by CMTW in their deliberations as they sought how to best articulate a policy for MTW on women serving in MTW. **Purpose of the Statement:** _“So God created man in His own image, in the image of God he created him;_ _male and female he created them. And God blessed them.”_ **Genesis 1:27-** **28a** _“In accordance with Scripture and the Reformed Confession, (is) the idea_ _that a human being does not bear or have the image of God, but that he or_ _she is the image of God”_ – Herman Bavinck, _Reformed Dogmatics: God and Creation_ CMTW’s statement calls our missional community to value all women, and to recognize and deploy women’s gifting in building the Church and extending the Kingdom of Jesus Christ around the world. In addition, our General Assembly through the Ad Interim Committee report has encouraged us to consider applicable recommendations from their report on “Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church,” amended and adopted by the 45 [th] General Assembly of the PCA. One aspect of the CMTW statement focuses on women in leadership roles in MTW. This leadership affirmation is part of CMTW’s encouragement to our missionary community to be “supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW’s global ministry.” As part of any discussion on leadership, we also affirm that all MTW leadership roles are based on a biblical model of servant leadership that does not seek to wield power over others, whether leadership is exercised by a man or a woman. MTW further recognizes that application of this portion of the statement regarding women serving in leadership roles in MTW may lead to specific and local questions of implementation, because of our shared desire to ensure that ecclesiastical authority over churches or church plants is reserved for men. Therefore, the Senior Leadership of MTW has endeavored to provide a list of considerations as a framework for thinking through application of this portion of the statement. **Recommendations from the 45** **[th]** **PCA General Assembly** [18] **:** These three recommendations from the adopted Recommendations from the Ad Interim Committee report are those that have particular applicability to our work in Mission to the World. 18 From the _Report of the Ad Interim Committee on Women serving in the Ministry of the_ _Church, to the 45_ _[th]_ _General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America_, as amended and adopted. **1. That sessions, presbyteries, and the General Assembly recognize** **that, from the founding of the PCA, there has been a variety of views** **and practices regarding the ways in which women may serve the** **Lord and the church within scriptural and constitutional** **parameters, without ordination, and that such mutual respect for** **said views and practices continues.** Rationale: The Scriptures and the constitution of the PCA state that offices of the church are only open to qualified and ordained men. But the committee also recognizes that the Scriptures and the constitution of the PCA give freedom to its churches with regard to varying views and practices by its churches in the ways in which women may serve the Lord and the church. This freedom of view and practice has also been part of the PCA’s history… Therefore, the committee recommends that ruling and teaching elders continue this recognition of freedom within PCA churches to utilize women’s gifts within the scriptural and constitutional parameters, without ordination. … this freedom of views and practices within PCA churches where Scripture and the constitution allow for freedom is a strength of the denomination and should be valued by the whole church. **2. That sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly strive to** **develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and** **wisdom of godly women in the local, regional, and national church,** **and particularly consider overtures that would allow qualified** **women to serve on appropriate committees and agencies within the** **church.** Rationale: The Scriptures teach that the Holy Spirit has given gifts to the church for the glory of God and the edification of the church (Rom. 12:38; 1 Cor. 12:1-11; Eph. 4:11- 16). Churches should strive to identify, develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom of all our members. … The committee further encourages PCA churches to utilize the gifts, skills, and knowledge of women by particularly and especially promoting and recruiting qualified women to serve. **3. That sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly consider how** **they can affirm and include underprivileged and underrepresented** **women in the PCA.** Rationale: After Jesus rose from the dead, He commanded His apostles: “Therefore, go make disciples of all nations” (Matt. 28:18). Jesus, our great King, prescribes the mission of His church, which, in part, is to ensure the nations become His disciples (cf. WCF 7.6). The overflow of the Great …

source: OVERTURE 42 from Chicago Metro Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Establish Study Committee on Sexuality” **Whereas**, in recent years a dramatic shift in cultural norms and attitudes away from Biblical teaching and morality concerning human sexuality has taken place; and **Whereas**, the current cultural climate presents an apologetic and evangelistic challenge to the Church as she seeks to articulate the Biblical teaching on human sexuality clearly and effectively to those outside; and **Whereas**, this cultural climate also fosters increasingly complex pastoral situations as the Church seeks to minister to those who struggle with issues related to their own sexuality; and **Whereas**, some of the flock in our midst are among those hard-pressed with temptation that manifests itself through same sex-attraction or a confused sexual identity, and many sessions may feel overwhelmed or underequipped to minister to them; and **Whereas**, though the PCA issued statements in 1977, 1996, and 1999 on the Biblical view concerning homosexuality, these statements were delivered before the more recent cultural changes with their attendant challenges, and the PCA has yet to undertake an extensive study of the topic; and **Whereas**, the PCA has the Biblical, theological, and confessional resources to apply the unchanging gospel to the issues surrounding human sexuality in our current cultural environment; **Therefore, be it resolved** that the 47 [th ] General Assembly create an Ad Interim Committee (AIC) to study the topic of human sexuality with particular attention to the issues of homosexuality, same- sex attraction, and transgenderism, and prepare a report which: - Shall include an annotated bibliography of resources on sexuality which the Committee endorses to help pastors and sessions shepherd congregants who are dealing with same-sex attraction; and - Shall address: (1) the nature of temptation, sin, and repentance as regards same sex- attraction; (2) the propriety of using terms like “gay Christian” when referring to a believer struggling with samesex attraction; (3) the status of "orientation" as a valid anthropological category; (4) the practice of “spiritual friendship” among same sex attracted Christians; and - Shall include suggested ways to articulate and defend a Biblical understanding of homosexuality, same sex-attraction, and transgenderism in the context of a culture that denies that understanding; and - Should the Committee conclude it prudent, may, as one of its recommendations, propose a statement on the topic; and **Be it further resolved,** that, in its examination of [20] Scripture and the PCA _Confession of Faith_ and Catechisms, the Committee consider studies and statements of other bodies outside and within the PCA (including, but not limited to, the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood’s “Nashville Statement”; the RPCNA’s “Contemporary Perspectives on Sexual Orientation: A Theological and Pastoral Analysis”; the RPCES’ “Pastoral Care for the Repentant Homosexual”; Missouri Presbytery’s “Homosexuality and the Gospel of Grace: Faithfulness to the Lord’s Calling in an Age of Sexual Autonomy”; the statements on homosexuality issued by the 5 [th], 24 [th], and 27 [th ] General Assemblies of the PCA and the January 14, 2015, Report of the CMC Subcommittee on Homosexuality) and resources recommended in those documents; and **Be it further resolved** that the Moderator of the 47 [th ] General Assembly appoint the seven voting members who shall be either PCA teaching or PCA ruling elders, and the Committee shall include at least two teaching and two ruling elders including members whose writings reflect theological engagement on the issue and pastoral interaction with those dealing with same sex attraction and transgenderism; and **Be it further resolved** that the Committee be permitted to recruit others to serve the Committee as advisors within the confines of its budget, with 20 The Ohio presbytery version here reads “that in addition to Scripture and the PCA _Confession of Faith_ and Catechisms….” Trinity’s Session made the small amendment to “in its examination of…” particular concern to secure advisors with experience in counseling those dealing with same-sex attraction and transgenderism; and **Be it further resolved** that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall present its report to the 48 [th ] General Assembly, including any recommendations it may present. _Adopted by Chicago Metro Presbytery at its stated meeting, May 15, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Kyle Edwards, stated clerk_

source: OVERTURE 43 from Metro Atlanta Presbytery (to AC, OC)
body: “Formation of a Study Committee on Domestic Abuse and Sexual Assault” (Version 8) **Whereas**, the sins of domestic abuse, including physical, emotional, and verbal abuse, and sexual assault are expressly forbidden in scripture (Deuteronomy 22:25-27; Eph. 5:25-29; 2 Timothy 3:2-5; 1 Peter 3:7; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; also WLC 135 and 139); and **Whereas**, these sins are especially heinous because they are “against the express letter of the law,” “break many commandments,” “admit of no reparation,” and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and **Whereas**, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society as well as the Church; and **Whereas**, these sins cause a complex set of physical, emotional, spiritual, and psychological responses—including immense shame, fear and anxiety, depression, trauma, isolation, anger, and denial—that persist with varying levels of severity throughout life; and since these heinous sins do lasting damage to every aspect of a victims life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and **Whereas**, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for the vulnerable and those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance in each case in accordance with applicable law (Ezekiel 34:1-24; James 1:27; BCO 8-3; 27-4); and **Whereas**, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations (cf. the Roman Catholic Church and the Southern Baptist Convention) but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly of the PCA; and **Whereas**, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and **Whereas**, the PCA report on “Divorce and Remarriage” was limited in its focus and does not adequately define the scope and nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault nor adequately address many pastoral concerns regarding the care of those victimized by such sins; and **Whereas**, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and **Whereas**, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and **Whereas**, the Rules of Discipline protect against unjust accusation ( _BCO_ 31 8), they also make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; **Therefore, be it resolved** that Metro Atlanta Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study: (1) the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for justly and lawfully protecting against these sins, for providing safety for potential victims who come forward, and for responding to those guilty of these sins; and (2) the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and (3) the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins as well as ministry and counsel for those guilty of such sins; (4) the possible need for repentance as a church; and (5) to include in their report a definition of the scope and nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and **Be it further resolved** that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with **Metro Atlanta** Presbytery committed to offer $ **1,000** ; and **Be it further resolved** that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for consideration by the 48th General Assembly. _Adopted by Metro Atlanta Presbytery at its stated meeting, May 7, 2019_ _Attested by /s/ TE Randy Schlichting, stated clerk_

(3) The status of "orientation" as a valid anthropological category; (4) the practice of “spiritual friendship” among same sex attracted Christians; and - Shall include suggested ways to articulate and defend a Biblical understanding of homosexuality, same sex-attraction, transgenderism, and gender dysphoria in the context of a culture that denies that understanding; and - Should the Committee conclude it prudent, may, as one of its recommendations, propose a statement on the topic; and **Be it further resolved,** that, in addition to Scripture and the PCA Confession of Faith and Catechisms, the Committee consider studies and statements of other bodies outside and within the PCA (including, but not limited to, the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood’s “Nashville Statement”; the statements on homosexuality issued by the 5 [th], 24 [th], and 27 [th] General Assemblies of the PCA and the January 14, 2015, Report of the CMC Subcommittee on Homosexuality) and resources recommended in those documents;
